Using 177 validated canonical artifacts, SERIAL-7 separates semantic derivation (Derive), constrained artifact generation (Realize), and cross-representation preservation (Preserve). Its 43 atomic representation constraints are paired with executable checks over format, structure, and task-specific semantics, enabling progressively stricter verification from representation compliance to full artifact validity. Across ten models, REALIZE-L3 HSR ranges from 42.0% to 93.9%, while Full Compliance exposes additional artifact-level failures beyond correct final answers and valid representations. These results show that reliable structured generation requires explicit, executable verification of how artifacts are realized and preserved across representations.
nodes.subject: Computation and Language

nodes.title: From Transcription to Reformulation: Defining and Benchmarking Grounded Generative Speech Recognition
nodes.authors: Qing Wang, Qihan Hu, Hang Lv, Yan Yang, Boqing Liu, Xuechao Zhu, Zehan Li, Hongjie Chen, Jian Kang, Jie Li, Yongxiang Li, Lei Xie
nodes.summary: Speech language models have expanded automatic speech recognition (ASR) from transcription to general speech-to-text generation. Yet existing benchmarks still assume a single ground-truth transcript per utterance, an assumption that struggles when models produce readable, formatted, or structured outputs. In this work, we introduce Grounded Generative Speech Recognition (GSR), reformulating speech recognition as generating semantically grounded text instead of a single transcript. We define a grounded reformulation space that characterizes all valid textual realizations supported by the input speech, and establish a four-level hierarchy of reformulation capabilities, including literal transcription, canonical reformulation, semantic reformulation and speech-grounded structuring. Based on this formulation, we present GSR-Bench, the first comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate generative speech recognition systems beyond exact transcript matching. GSR-Bench covers diverse scenarios including refined meeting transcription, cross-dialect translation, context-aware speech understanding, and robustness under silent or noisy acoustic conditions. To address the limitations of word-level evaluation metrics, we develop a multi-dimensional evaluation framework combining speech grounding assessment and LLM-based semantic judgment, whose reliability is validated through human preference studies. Extensive experiments across representative architectures, ranging from conventional ASR systems to end-to-end Speech-LLMs, reveal fundamental trade-offs between transcription fidelity and generative reformulation ability. Our analysis further identifies critical failure modes, including acoustic hallucination, unsupported generation, and instruction drift, providing insights into the design and evaluation of future grounded generative speech systems.
nodes.subject: Computation and Language

nodes.title: In-Model Context Compression with Agentic Soft Tokens for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
nodes.authors: Xuning He, Kai Fan, Runyu Zhang, Binghuan Wang, Yuxiang Zhang, Xue Jiang, Yihong Dong
nodes.summary: Long-horizon LLM agents play an important role in solving complex and sustained tasks, with ever-growing interaction contexts. However, these accumulated contexts will raise substantial computational cost and obscure key decision-relevant evidence. Existing methods typically train external compressors or context-management agents to rewrite context as shorter hard-token sequences, but such external selection may not align with the LLM's evolving representation and is necessarily lossy. In this paper, we introduce Agentic Soft-Token Compression (ASTC), a training-free compression method using soft tokens within LLM agent for long-horizon tasks. Specifically, ASTC uses the model's native recurrent dynamics to determine the already absorbed information, leveraging the commonly-used hybrid Gated Delta Network (GDN)-attention. It then carries this information forward as agentic soft tokens while retaining exact values as hard tokens. The resulting compact sequence reduces later-layer computation and yields reusable KV caches, extending the savings across the agent's trajectory. Extensive experiments on long-horizon tasks show that ASTC matches or exceeds the uncompressed agent's accuracy with up to 50.68% fewer end-to-end Attention Pairs, while trained compressors require 15.4 to 103.7 times more Attention Pairs per successful task. These findings highlight agentic soft tokens as a model-native way to carry absorbed context forward as the task representation evolves.
nodes.subject: Computation and Language

nodes.title: PsyInterviewee: Informational Invariance and Relational Adaptivity in Mental Health Interview Simulation
nodes.authors: Jiawei Zhang, Huachuan Qiu, Ruocheng Guo, Zijun Shi
nodes.summary: LLM-based simulated interviewees support interviewer training and the evaluation of mental health interviewing systems. Existing studies have primarily focused on improving human-likeness through richer patient profiles and behavioral modeling. However, human-likeness alone does not establish their reliability. Reliable simulation requires preserving profile-grounded clinical facts (informational invariance) while adapting disclosure and interaction behavior to the interview (relational adaptivity). To this end, we introduce PsyInterviewee, which separates a protected truth channel from a dynamic interaction channel and verifies generated clinical claims against the profile. Specifically, asymmetric write permissions allow dialogue context to update disclosure and behavioral states without authorizing new clinical facts; these states guide what profile-supported information is revealed and how it is expressed. In an automated evaluation of interactions between LLM-based interviewers and interviewees, PsyInterviewee achieves higher scores than four representative baselines on most metrics across both axes, as assessed by two LLM judges. Ablations suggest that the two channels contribute to clinical grounding and response modulation, respectively.
nodes.subject: Computation and Language

nodes.title: SciGraphSelect: Auditable Scientific Data Selection through Knowledge--Reasoning Graphs
nodes.authors: MiHyeon Kim, Ji-Eun Han, Eunkyeong Lee, Jeehyun Lim, Hwijung Ryu
nodes.summary: Scientific data selection is typically driven by relevance or utility scores, providing limited insight into why a document is retained. We introduce SciGraphSelect, a reference-grounded framework for auditable scientific data selection. SciGraphSelect organizes domain-specific knowledge, reusable reasoning operations, and reference-attested relations into a typed knowledge--reasoning graph, then scores candidate documents using concept coverage, relation and path co-support, and directional alignment. To avoid over-interpreting document embeddings, rich relational structure is preserved on the reference side while candidate-side evidence is treated conservatively without assuming relation entailment. By exposing the reference-grounded evidence behind each selection, SciGraphSelect brings traceability to the upstream construction of scientific training corpora and complements downstream scientific verification.
nodes.subject: Computation and Language

nodes.title: TRIDENT and SHAKTI: A Framework and Benchmark for Hindi AI-Text Detection
nodes.authors: Shifali Agrahari, Sujit Kumar, Sanasam Ranbir Singh
nodes.summary: As Large Language Models (LLMs) become increasingly multilingual, distinguishing human-written from AI-generated text is essential for maintaining information integrity. However, research remains English-centric, with limited benchmarks for low-resource languages such as Hindi. To address this gap, we introduce SHAKTI, a large-scale Hindi benchmark covering four genres, eight LLM families, multiple prompting strategies, and adversarial transformations. We evaluate its quality through human annotation and analyze linguistic, grammatical, and sentiment-based differences between human- and AI-generated texts. Building on these findings, we propose TRIDENT, a round-trip translation-based detection framework with three variants: TRIDENT-S (static threshold), TRIDENT-D (dynamic threshold), and TRIDENT-C (logistic regression using multi-distance RTT features). TRIDENT leverages semantic consistency between original and round-trip translated texts to identify AI-generated content. Extensive experiments show that TRIDENT outperforms conventional and supervised baselines, with TRIDENT-S achieving the best overall performance. Further evaluations across seven languages, adversarial settings, and unseen LLMs demonstrate its multilingual applicability and robustness, while highlighting sensitivity to the translation model.
nodes.subject: Computation and Language

nodes.title: Beyond Response Scoring: An AI-aware Cognitive Supervision Framework for Automated Mathematical Short Answer Grading
nodes.authors: Shengran Guo, Min Chi, Feifei Qiao, Varad Patwardhan
nodes.summary: Transformer-based language models have achieved remarkable success in automated short answer grading (ASAG). However, current methods in ASAG struggle to comprehend, reason about and evaluate complex mathematical answers involving symbols and formulas. These score-only methods fail to generalize across diverse responses and skill states associated with identical scores. Moreover, they ignore the potential upward bias introduced by generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) usage in assessing students' performance and knowledge mastery. To address these limitations, we propose AICG (AI-aware Cognitive-supervised Grading), a two-branch multi-task framework. The first branch combines RoBERTa-based regression, ordinal, and classification heads for individual-answer grading. The second branch uses an expert-designed Q-matrix to associate responses with assessed skills and jointly predicts G-DINA-derived skill mastery and learning gain. Through the shared encoder, these skill-level targets provide cognitive supervision for answer grading beyond score labels. AICG further uses a Gen-AI detector, trained through supervised contrastive pretraining followed by linear classification, to estimate assistance probabilities and convert them into reliability weights, attenuating unreliable cognitive evidence during learning assessment. We conduct experiments on 49,402 instructor-graded responses spanning 19 academic semesters. Relative to RoBERTa regression, AICG reduces mean absolute error (MAE) by 50.3% and improves quadratic weighted kappa (QWK) from 0.798 to 0.927. Ablations identify Q-matrix-guided cognitive supervision as the primary source of improvement, while AI-aware weighting further reduces overall MAE by 4.2% over the unweighted cognitive model and consistently improves MAE and QWK across the four most recent post-Gen-AI semesters.
nodes.subject: Computation and Language

nodes.title: TraceSpec: Understanding and Improving Speculative Decoding for LLM Agents
nodes.authors: Jihao Zhao, Shuaishuai Zu, Pengfei Li, Biao Qin, Guanghuan Fang, Ben Feng, Baochuan Yang
nodes.summary: LLM agents execute tasks through repeated model calls over evolving histories of reasoning, actions, and tool feedback. Aggregate speculative-decoding metrics merge these distinct decisions, providing limited guidance on where draft supervision is needed. We present TraceSpec, a framework connecting trajectory evaluation with adaptive draft training. It combines dynamic execution with fixed-prefix replay and introduces TraceSpec-Traj, a corpus of 10,000 training states and 2,500 test states spanning browsing and software engineering. Analysis of five speculative baselines reveals that aggregate acceptance can rise with context length while declining within matched late browsing actions. Workload and phase further distinguish these trends, motivating supervision guided by trajectory conditions. TraceSpec trains on intermediate assistant turns and allocates a fixed prediction budget using state-conditioned estimates of prefix-aware acceptance gaps. Across three target sizes and two temperatures, it improves replay throughput by 12.5% to 22.6% over its DSpark base. Qwen3-4B ablations show that adaptive allocation increases accepted length by 3.3% to 10.0% over fixed full-turn supervision, with additional comparisons substantiating the roles of state conditioning and consecutive-token agreement. The resulting evaluation resources, trajectory findings, and training strategy connect the analysis of agent execution to practical draft improvement.
nodes.subject: Computation and Language

nodes.title: S2TDR: Structured Multimodal Reconstruction for Sticker-Aware Dialogue Understanding
nodes.authors: Yuanchen Shi, Fang Kong
nodes.summary: Stickers are widely used in social media dialogues to express affect, stance, and intent beyond literal text. Their meanings are often non-literal and context-dependent, making them difficult to handle with generic visual fusion or standalone captioning. We propose Sticker-to-Text Dialogue Reconstruction (S2TDR), a structured multimodal reconstruction framework that converts sticker turns into contextually appropriate textual utterances. S2TDR decomposes sticker interpretation into visual cue extraction, affective-intent inference, and context-aware dialogue reconstruction, using OCR text only as an auxiliary cue when available. The reconstructed dialogue can then be consumed by existing text-based dialogue models. Experiments on sentiment analysis, intent recognition, and dialogue summarization show that S2TDR generally improves multiple downstream models over direct sticker integration methods. Further analyses on component ablations, OCR-empty stickers, and reconstruction quality indicate that structured reconstruction provides an interpretable and effective way to integrate sticker semantics into dialogue understanding.
nodes.subject: Computation and Language

nodes.title: Context as Infrastructure: Knowledge Compilation for Retrieval in Agentic Systems with Harnesses
nodes.authors: Zhichang Yu, Baining Cao, Sbaaoui Idriss, Qi Wang, Gangqiang Xu, Ling Qin, Xiaoling Jin, An Liu, Shaohao Cai, Xiaoyang Bao, Shengle Chen, Changchang Ding, Pengfei Zhu, Jingxiang Xu, Yifeng Mao, Lu Liu, Hai Jin, Yingfeng Zhang
nodes.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation is becoming agentic. A search harness writes queries, reads results, reformulates, and decides when to stop. This largely solves accuracy: a harness with only BM25/grep and MiniMax M3 answers 85% of BrowseComp-Plus and 91% on multi-hop FRAMES in our runs, without compiled or vector indexes. It exposes a context problem: an undisciplined loop repeats queries, rereads documents, and fills the window with unused passages. The missing layer is knowledge compilation: a configurable ingestion pipeline where LLMs enrich documents with context no chunk contains alone--navigation hierarchies with claim-evidence leaves, entity graphs, timelines, mind maps, ontologies, wikis, and memory. Compilation is not a better retriever: under a competent harness, structural artifacts gave no detectable accuracy gain on FRAMES, and a PageIndex-style outline degraded at scale. It is a supply layer. A navigation tree whose leaves are claim-evidence pairs--the mechanism we measure--cuts query tokens by 91% when evidence suffices and adds 1.9% when it does not, a 38% average reduction; this implies a 2% break-even sufficiency rate and a measured rate near 43%. A decision gate cuts latency from 140 s to 30 s, though substitution's token saving is bought with retrieval rounds and carries its own latency cost. Other artifacts--ontology, graph, wiki, timeline, mind map, memory--pay off in deployment (governance, integration, onboarding, temporal orientation, continuity) where accuracy benchmarks cannot see them. We describe RAGFlow's pipeline and harness (open source at https://github.com/infiniflow/ragflow), which turns the loop into five disciplined stations and keeps the context entering the model the smallest sufficient set; together they form an agent-native database: a store that hands the agent compiled, governed context instead of a ranked list of passages.
nodes.subject: Computation and Language

nodes.title: Lineage Is Memory: Parent Inheritance and Feedback Disclosure in Short-Budget LLM-Guided Optimization
nodes.authors: Shanglin Yang, Zhan Shi
nodes.summary: Iterative language-model optimizers refine prompts and programs by evaluating a candidate, showing a proposer model a sample of failing cases, and keeping revisions that improve performance. Recent work attributes the limits of this loop to narrow single-round reflection, introducing full-set error clustering, targeted minibatches, or larger proposer models so the optimizer sees more failure modes per step. Yet every existing evaluation tests these mechanisms exclusively inside lineage-preserving search, where each revision edits a surviving parent, leaving the contribution of parent inheritance confounded with the breadth of per-round feedback. Across 1,750 pre-registered runs spanning nine prompt and program synthesis benchmarks, we separate parent inheritance from feedback disclosure under matched evaluation budgets. We find that greedy parent inheritance drives the vast majority of optimization progress, outperforming seed-reset resampling even when seed-reset proposals receive a clustered summary of all failures in every round or use a larger proposer model. While full-set error clustering and diverse failure selection improve single-step rewrites from the seed and accelerate the opening rounds of search, sequential parent inheritance rapidly closes this gap as solved error modes are retained in the candidate and filtered from subsequent failure lists. Moreover, decomposing token expenditure in GEPA reveals that proposer reflection accounts for only a small fraction of total cost whereas validation and minibatch gating consume nearly the entire budget, showing that greedy parent inheritance over raw failures captures the gains of complex reflective loops at a fraction of their compute.
nodes.subject: Computation and Language

nodes.title: HyperRepair: Recovering Forgotten General Capabilities of Fine-Tuned Language Models
nodes.authors: Junrong Tang, Jianghui Wang, Hao Kong, Yang Lin, Yibo Yang
nodes.summary: Fine-tuning improves a language model's performance in a target domain but can weaken its general capabilities. Existing methods often face a trade-off between general capabilities and domain specialization, making it difficult to preserve both. We introduce HyperRepair, a framework for recovering general capabilities while retaining domain specialization at only inference cost. To make recovery generalizable across models sharing a pretrained backbone, HyperRepair learns a hypernetwork from repairs trained on source models. The hypernetwork uses activation fingerprints that summarize changes from the pretrained backbone to generate a tailored Repairing Side Net (RSN), whose prompt-conditioned gate applies corrections selectively. This enables recovery on models from unseen adaptation domains without target-domain examples or additional optimization. We evaluate HyperRpair across two model families, 12 LoRA adaptation datasets, and 15 general benchmarks. On the default split, HyperRepair achieves 93.4% of the base models' average general score while retaining 99.5% of the fine-tuned models' average domain score.
nodes.subject: Computation and Language

nodes.title: Language Models Show a "Women-Are-Wonderful" Effect in Blame Attribution That is Not Just Leniency
nodes.authors: Anika Sharma, Snehalkumar 'Neil' S. Gaikwad, Snigdha Chaturvedi, Shashank Srivastava
nodes.summary: This paper investigates the Women-Are-Wonderful (WaW) effect in language-model blame attribution: a favorable bias in which women receive more positive evaluations than men. Using 11,270 interpersonal conflicts from r/AmItheAsshole, we construct matched counterfactuals that vary the gender of the person being judged (the original poster) and the person affected (the counter-party). Across four language models, gender changes a minority of verdicts, but those changes consistently favor women. The effect is strongly role-dependent. Making the original poster a woman reduces the odds of blame by 9--52%, while making the counter-party a woman multiplies them by 2.7--9.2X. Counter-party WaW also varies across conflict types, strengthening in communication and relationship conflicts and weakening in family conflicts. Exploratory probes suggest that counter-party gender can shift judgments of sympathy, reasonableness, harm and protection. WaW is therefore not just leniency toward women being judged: models also judge conduct more harshly when it affects a woman.
nodes.subject: Computation and Language

nodes.title: MUON-RT Reusing the Teacher's Trajectory for Momentum-Free Muon for LLM Self-Distillation
nodes.authors: Aryan Das, Vinay Kumar Verma, Aakansha Mishra
nodes.summary: Self-distillation methods for large language models with an exponential moving average (EMA) teacher already retain a history of student updates. Muon nevertheless stores a separate momentum buffer, increasing persistent training memory. We propose Muon with Reused Teacher (Muon-RT), which reuses the teacher-student displacement to eliminate momentum buffers for hidden weight matrices. We show that this displacement encodes an exponentially weighted history of applied updates and smooths temporally uncorrelated noise under a local model. Muon-RT removes its radial component, normalizes it spectrally, and mixes it with the current gradient after Newton-Schulz (NS) orthogonalization. Under explicit regularity and alignment assumptions, we establish linear contraction of an expected objective-gap bound toward a residual error level. With Self-Distillation Fine-Tuning (SDFT) on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Muon-RT improves average accuracy over AdamW by 2.6 points with 42% less persistent memory, and over momentum Muon by 5.4 points with 27% less persistent memory. With Self-Distillation Policy Optimization (SDPO) on Olmo-3-7B-Instruct, it improves average accuracy over AdamW by 2.0 points.
nodes.subject: Computation and Language

nodes.title: Search When Needed, Proceed When Reliable: Metacognitive Reliability Supervision for Efficient Agentic Search
nodes.authors: Minhao Sun, Zhijing Wu, Xian-Ling Mao
nodes.summary: Efficient agentic search requires large language models (LLMs) to determine whether they can reliably proceed with their current knowledge or need additional external evidence. Supervision based on final-answer correctness or trajectory-level feedback evaluates realized trajectory performance. However, observed trajectory performance is jointly shaped by stochastic generation, retrieval quality, and downstream reasoning. Such signals therefore provide only indirect evidence of how reliable the current decision state was and how retrieved evidence changed its reliability. An effective reward should encourage search when external information is needed and favor searches that contribute to the answer. To this end, we propose a metacognitive framework for training LLMs to make search decisions based on the reliability of their intermediate reasoning states. Our framework estimates the reliability of local conclusions to distinguish whether the current information supports proceeding without search from how much retrieved evidence improves that reliability. The current-state reliability score assesses whether the model can proceed without search. The search-action score measures how retrieved evidence changes estimated reliability. Together, these scores define a reliability-aware process reward for Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), providing finer-grained supervision for search and no-search behavior. Experiments across seven question-answering benchmarks demonstrate that our method achieves a better accuracy-efficiency trade-off than strong agentic-search baselines. Our code and model checkpoints will be open-sourced.
nodes.subject: Information Retrieval

nodes.title: KITE: Retrieval as a Decision Procedure for Long-Term Conversational Memory
nodes.authors: Feng Li, Kailun Tan, Zhibo Zhou, Youxiang Wang, Lejun Liu, Huaigu Li, Fei Du, Huilong An
nodes.summary: Many long-term memory systems for LLM agents are built around embedding-based retrieval. Al- though effective for semantic matching, similarity ranking alone does not establish whether re- trieved memories satisfy the conditions implied by a question. In this paper, we introduce KITE (Knowledge-Indexed Temporal Evidence), a vector-free framework that formulates memory re- trieval as an explicit decision procedure. KITE organizes multi-session conversations as structured knowledge indexed by a governed topic vocabulary, which evolves through controlled expansion and consolidation. At query time, questions are compiled into inspectable retrieval plans over the same knowledge index that guides memory construction. The plans are then executed through fixed lookup and ranking operations, while sparse lexical retrieval recovers surface details omitted from the structured representation. Experiments on LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S show that KITE achieves 93.5% and 86.0% accuracy while using only about 1.6k reader-context tokens per ques- tion. These results demonstrate that conversational memory can move beyond similarity ranking by unifying memory construction and query compilation around a governed index, turning retrieval into an inspectable decision procedure for determining which evidence satisfies the question.
nodes.subject: Information Retrieval

nodes.title: How BERT-based Cross-Encoders Model Relevance in Information Retrieval?
nodes.authors: Mathias Vast, Basile Van Cooten, Laure Soulier, Benjamin Piwowarski
nodes.summary: Cross-encoders are the most effective but also the least efficient models in Information Retrieval. Despite their success, the mechanisms underlying their relevance predictions remain poorly understood, particularly how they process to match queries and documents. This lack of interpretability limits their optimization, can lead to suboptimal retrieval, especially out-of-domain, and raises efficiency concerns for over-parameterized models. To address these challenges, this paper investigates two under-explored aspects of cross-encoder behavior. First, to understand the relevance prediction process, we trace the flow of information at the different stages of the process and between different input segments. We study the nature of the signals that compose this flow and that allow cross-encoders to predict the relevance of a passage to a query. Our work particularly focuses on the matching performed by the cross-encoders between queries and documents. Second, we explore how cross-encoders behave with out-of-domain documents and/or queries. Through a series of interpretability experiments, we evaluate three BERT-based cross-encoder models, varying in size and pre-training strategies, across both in-domain and out-of-domain datasets. Overall, this study both consolidates what is known about how cross-encoders model relevance and extends it by exploring the role of matching signals.
nodes.subject: Information Retrieval

nodes.title: Fidelity Synopses: Pre-Execution Plan Selection for Approximate Vector Search
nodes.authors: Adithya Ramanatha, Sanskar S. Singh, Maya Ramanath
nodes.summary: Vector search has become a database operator with many physical implementations: different index families, build-time and search-time parameters, and compressed or disk-resident variants. Each trades cost against fidelity, the fraction of a query's exact top-k nearest neighbors that a configuration returns. Deployments nevertheless choose one configuration offline and use it for every query, so they are sized for their hardest queries and overpay for the rest. On a 5.8M-item LAION benchmark with four embedding models, running each query on the cheapest configuration that suffices for it would roughly halve the cost in a typical setting. Exploiting this requires predicting each configuration's fidelity before running it, which is hard because fidelity is defined by the very exact search that approximate indexes avoid. Relational optimizers solve the analogous problem for cardinality with offline synopses; we propose one for vector search. A fidelity synopsis divides the embedding space into cells around a set of landmarks and records, for every cell and configuration, how often that configuration met a fidelity target on a sample of queries. At query time, one nearest-landmark lookup yields a calibrated estimate for every configuration, and an optimizer chooses configurations so that the workload misses the target no more often than its requirement allows. We test the two premises the synopsis relies on, that fidelity varies smoothly across the embedding space and that its loss is specific to each configuration. Held to the same requirement a static deployment is built to meet, synopsis-guided selection lowers cost in all 16 combinations of model and query direction, to a median of 0.72x the static deployment, with a batched lookup of 21-32 microseconds per query. The saving persists against the best static choice among the same indexes, and within a single index at no extra memory.
nodes.subject: Information Retrieval

nodes.title: Hierarchical Dual-Graph Retrieval for Long-form Audio Reasoning
nodes.authors: Eunsang Lee, Taein Ju, Jiyoung Lee
nodes.summary: Large audio language models (LALMs) struggle with long-form audio reasoning, as processing entire recordings often limits to capture query-relevant content distributed across distant segments while incurring substantial computational cost. We introduce AudioHelix, a hierarchical DualGraph framework tailored for LALMs' retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems. Unlike existing text-only or non-graph RAG approaches, AudioHelix connects related textual and acoustic evidence across temporally distant segments for multi-hop reasoning. Extensive experiments on TraceAV-Bench, MMAU-Pro, and AudioMarathon demonstrate that AudioHelix consistently outperforms full-audio processing and existing RAG methods. The project site is https://github.com/ewha-mmai/audiohelix.
nodes.subject: Information Retrieval

nodes.title: BrowseFlow: Sparse Event Flow Matching for Generative User Simulation
nodes.authors: Yitian Pang, Jiayi Zhang, Zhenjia Ma, Xiaowei Yue, Dagui Chen, Jian Xu
nodes.summary: User simulation aims to reproduce how users interact with content and products across online platforms. Recent generative approaches have enriched user simulation with behavioral history and contextual information. However, realistic browsing simulation still faces two challenges. (i) Stochastic Responses: Even with the same recommendation feed, the same user may produce different browsing responses, yielding distinct behavioral trajectories. A logged trajectory records only one such realization. (ii) Sparse Key Events: Clicks and likes provide important feedback but occur sparsely within browsing trajectories dominated by progression actions such as scrolling. Many stepwise simulators predict these actions in a dense sequence, where key events contribute relatively few training targets. To address these challenges, we propose BrowseFlow, a conditional discrete flow matching method for generative user simulation. For Sparse Key Events, BrowseFlow represents each response by its browsing extent and an ordered sequence of key events, directly modeling their counts and locations under exposure constraints. BrowseFlow learns the conditional distribution of complete browsing responses through probabilistic extent prediction and discrete flow matching over key events. Random event retention defines probability paths over partial event sequences, while transition rate matching learns stochastic insertion dynamics. For Stochastic Responses, we use the energy score, a proper scoring rule, to evaluate response fidelity and generated variability, complemented by the Wasserstein distance between key event count distributions. We further introduce TaobaoBrowse, a benchmark pairing real recommendation contexts with fine-grained browsing trajectories. Experiments across three datasets demonstrate that BrowseFlow consistently achieves the best distributional performance.
nodes.subject: Information Retrieval

nodes.title: Defining Page-Centric Visual Document Retrieval and Evaluating Existing Benchmarks
nodes.authors: Chongzhi Zhang, Yuqi Zuo, Aixin Sun
nodes.summary: In modern information retrieval (IR), documents are increasingly encountered as structured sequences of visually rich, paginated units, rather than as flat text. Example documents encountered in our daily life include Word files, PDFs, and slide decks. Free text-centric retrieval systems either ignore this structure entirely or destroy it through arbitrary passage chunking. In this paper, we formulate page-centric Visual Document Retrieval (VDR) with pages as the fundamental indexing units and document context available for assessing page relevance. The formulation distinguishes two retrieval granularities, page and document, and three retrieval paradigms: independent-item, evidence-set, and iterative retrieval. We then assess 42 benchmarks using eight criteria covering corpus characteristics, query construction, relevance annotation, and ranking support. Our analysis shows two main findings on current VDR research. First, evaluation remains concentrated on page-level independent-item retrieval, with fewer resources supporting document-level, evidence-set, and iterative settings. Second, queries originating from real user information needs independently of target corpus content and graded relevance judgments are uncommon, while the coverage and verification of relevance judgments vary substantially. Both findings reveal gaps between the capabilities applications require and those existing evaluation protocols can establish. We provide benchmark selection guidance and identify priorities for future benchmark design, emphasizing alignment between task requirements, relevance semantics, and evaluation protocols.
nodes.subject: Information Retrieval

nodes.title: Pix2Evidence: A Multimodal RAG System for Text and Visual Evidence
nodes.authors: Ziniu Liu, Xiaoyang Chen, Dezhi Ye, Jie Liu, Jin Ma, Hao Deng
nodes.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) over visually rich documents must find both relevant content and the evidence that supports an answer. Screenshot retrieval preserves images and page structure, but written facts within screenshots also need to be searchable. Moreover, topical relevance alone does not identify which retrieved tile contains evidence for the answer. We introduce Pix2Evidence, a multimodal RAG system that encodes each screenshot tile together with its available transcription into a single fused image--text representation, so that layout and readable text are considered jointly during retrieval. To guide evidence selection, a vision-language teacher describes the visible content that supports each training question. We use these descriptions to adapt the retriever, then rerank the retrieved candidates before answer generation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Pix2Evidence outperforms state-of-the-art methods. Across five widely-used Wikipedia QA benchmarks, the non-reranked Pix2Evidence leads the main comparison in answer accuracy on four. On MMSearch, it reaches 26.0\%, 4.4 percentage points above PixelRAG. We will release the code and share derived data where licensing and privacy reviews permit.
nodes.subject: Information Retrieval

nodes.title: MILES-Rec: Uncovering Implicit Intents from Mobility Behaviors for Cross-Domain POI Recommendation
nodes.authors: Yi Zou, Wei Luo, Xuewen Zhang, Zhuang Yan, Pengjie Wang
nodes.summary: Map applications bridge everyday mobility with local services, creating opportunities to recommend places by uncovering users' implicit intents. However, utility-driven map interactions provide only indirect and incomplete evidence of consumption demands, making it challenging to infer personalized service needs from observed behaviors. We propose MILES-Rec, a cross-domain POI recommendation framework that infers latent service intents from heterogeneous map behaviors and expresses them as prioritized natural language queries. It first learns from progressive reasoning demonstrations that synthesize user profiles and map histories for situation understanding, intent expansion, and query prioritization. We then introduce intent-aligned group relative policy optimization, using subsequent user interactions to reward query relevance and ranked service coverage while penalizing redundancy and excessive response length. A two-level credit assignment mechanism integrates shared list-level advantages with query-specific advantages, coordinating individual query quality with the complementary coverage of the complete query list. We further construct MILES-Bench from real user interaction logs on a large-scale mapping platform, supporting training and evaluation across diverse services under rich and sparse behavioral histories. Extensive experiments against general-purpose LLMs and specialized recommendation baselines demonstrate superior POI retrieval utility and strong service and semantic alignment, with consistent gains from behavioral policy optimization across four backbone scales.
nodes.subject: Information Retrieval

nodes.title: MEMENTO: Learning Context Management for Long Context Processing Agents
nodes.authors: Yunfan Zhang, Taehoon Hwang, Kathleen McKeown, Smaranda Muresan
nodes.summary: LLM agents that operate over long inputs must perform context management: deciding what to retain in a fixed-size context window. A common approach is compaction, where the model replaces its history with a self-generated note. Yet off-the-shelf agentic models, including GPT-5.5 and GLM-5.3, often write ineffective notes, and reinforcement learning (RL) alone rarely discovers useful note-taking behavior. We present MEMENTO, a long-context agent built on Qwen3-8B and trained to manage its context through compaction. We first bootstrap note-taking by fine-tuning on synthetic trajectories annotated with notes generated in hindsight, then reinforce it with RL using a reward that combines answer correctness, note-quality heuristics, and confidence calibration. Although trained only to compact into a fresh window, MEMENTO extends at test time to strategies such as context folding and confidence-based backtracking. On book-level question answering across four benchmarks, with books of up to 2.5M tokens, MEMENTO raises Qwen3-8B's accuracy from 36.9% to 67.8% while never holding more than 20K tokens in context. It outperforms GPT-5.5 agent in the same harness (13.1%) and full book context (56.7%) at less than 1/50 the cost. It also nearly matches a ~100x larger GLM-5.3 agent (69.3%) at 1/9 the cost, and comes within 6.4 points of GLM-5.3 full context at 1/26 the cost.
nodes.subject: Information Retrieval

nodes.title: PatchScout: Thematic Web Data Collection via Information Foraging
nodes.authors: Michael West, Eduard Dragut
nodes.summary: Researchers often need web corpora that are not answers to a single query, but reusable collections of documents spanning many decentralized sources. We refer to this problem as thematic web data collection: assembling semantically relevant documents that share a common theme but are scattered across heterogeneous and structurally disconnected regions of the web. Existing approaches, including traversal-based methods and LLM-driven web agents, are limited by local exploration or short-horizon stopping, preventing comprehensive collection. We formulate this task as a long-horizon information foraging problem over query-induced semantic patches, where the central challenge is deciding when to continue local exploitation and when to switch to new regions. We propose PatchScout, a multi-agent framework that instantiates a class of patch-switching policies to balance local exploitation and adaptive patch switching under a fixed budget. Experiments on four live-web topics show that PatchScout substantially improves yield and domain coverage over traversal-based and search-augmented reasoning agent baselines. In an applied social science setting with an incomplete prior collection, PatchScout discovers 102 previously unidentified entities, illustrating its ability to expand existing thematic datasets.
nodes.subject: Information Retrieval

nodes.title: Fast Privacy Loss Accounting for Random Allocation via Multiscale FFT
nodes.authors: Vitaly Feldman, Moshe Shenfeld
nodes.summary: In the random allocation sampling scheme each user's data is used in $k$ steps chosen randomly and uniformly from a sequence of $t$ steps. This scheme is known to improve on Poisson sampling in private optimization and in communication-efficient aggregation. The existing privacy loss distribution (PLD) accountant for this scheme runs in time quadratic in the inverse of the accuracy parameter $α$ (Feldman and Shenfeld, 2026). We give an algorithm, \emph{multiscale FFT}, that represents likelihood ratios on a grid that is uniform within each dyadic interval and computes the exact rounding of every pairwise sum using FFTs within each interval. It keeps the guarantees of the accountant and improves the dependence of its running time on $α$ from $O(α^{-2})$ to $O(α^{-1}\log(1/α))$. In addition, we demonstrate that rounding can be performed via the mean-preserving connect-the-dots projection of (Doroshenko et al., 2026). This reduces the errors that rounding introduces in the mean of the privacy loss and in the $χ^2$ divergence of the computed pair from the order of $α$ to $O(α^2/\log(t))$. In our experiments, our algorithm achieves speedups of several orders of magnitude at high accuracy and gives improved privacy bounds for DP-SGD with PREAMBLE.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: Regret-Optimal Wasserstein-Robust Linear Regression
nodes.authors: Sloan Nietert, Daniel Kuhn
nodes.summary: Distributionally robust optimization (DRO) minimizes worst-case risk under distributional uncertainty, but its decisions can be suboptimal in terms of their excess risk, or regret. We study this gap for multivariate least-squares regression, assuming that the observed source law and unknown target law differ by an adversarial 2-Wasserstein perturbation of size $\varepsilon$. We first identify the asymptotic complexity of robust decision-making in the $\varepsilon \to 0$ limit, characterized by a problem-specific condition number $κ$. Here, a wide spectrum of simple algorithms, including DRO, achieve the instance-optimal rate of $O(κ\varepsilon^2)$. For fixed $\varepsilon > 0$, we prove that DRO still achieves the minimax rate if the problem has bounded residual effective rank. On the other hand, we identify significant failure modes where DRO is provably suboptimal by dimension-dependent factors. Fortunately, we prove that two alternative procedures, minimax regret optimization (MRO) and spectral-norm regularization (SNR), attain the minimax rate. We derive an exact convex reformulation of MRO and an accelerated proximal algorithm for SNR, along with high-probability finite-sample guarantees. We support these theoretical results with numerical experiments separating the performance of MRO and SNR from DRO.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: Cost-Aware Stopping for Freeze-Thaw Bayesian Optimization: When Does One-Step Lookahead Suffice?
nodes.authors: Long Vu, Jongseong Brad Choi, Binoy Ravindran, Zhoulai Fu
nodes.summary: Freeze-thaw Bayesian optimization (BO) evaluates candidates in resumable increments but usually stops at a budget or convergence test. We maximize a budget-free utility, the best observed score minus a cost per increment, with a one-step lookahead: advance the candidate with the largest expected improvement (EI) under a fixed surrogate, and stop once no EI exceeds the cost. This rule, EI stopping, never falls below stopping immediately in expected utility, yet it can stop too early. We construct a certificate, a lower bound on the value of two-step lookahead, that proves such a stop premature, and repeating this correction never lowers expected utility under the surrogate. Under the surrogate, EI stops are premature on average at low costs and lose little at high costs. On three hyperparameter optimization benchmarks, a pre-registered test finds EI stopping noninferior to the correction in most high-cost settings, while the correction gains at low costs on two of the three; more information sharing in the surrogate raises EI stopping's utility. On the surrogates of two published methods, EI stopping trades lower scores for fewer training increments. EI stopping is a simple cost-aware reference whose utility depends on the surrogate.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: Exact Theory and Optimal Stepsizes for Stochastic Gradient Descent in Smooth Convex Minimization
nodes.authors: Benjamin Grimmer, Qining Shen
nodes.summary: This work considers the design of stepsize schedules for stochastic gradient descent in smooth convex optimization. Throughout, we assume that gradient noise is conditionally zero-mean with bounded variance. Among problems with dimension $d\geq N+1$, we provide an exact worst-case analysis of the expected suboptimality of stochastic gradient descent's final iterate. Our analysis applies to any (potentially nonconstant) schedule of $N$ stepsizes in $[0,1.5]^N$. Here, exact means that we provide a matching objective function and noise distributions where our guarantee is attained. Whenever the variance bound is at least $Ω(1/\sqrt{N})$, our theory provides the minimax optimal stepsize schedule for stochastic gradient descent and proves its uniqueness. These optimal stepsizes monotonically decrease, ruling out any accelerations in expected final suboptimality from fixed fractal schedules observed in the deterministic case.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: A richness-sensitive Acoustic Biodiversity Index from species-level detections: classifier benchmarking, false-positive control and validation against standard soundscape indices in an African savanna and an urban zoo
nodes.authors: Muhammad Saeed, Dmitry Mikhaylov, Mohamed H. Alhosani, Yasser F. Al Wahedi, Rory Pilossof, Ahmed Arabi, Walid Shaaba
nodes.summary: Acoustic indices are widely used as rapid proxies for biodiversity, but they summarise the distribution of sound energy rather than the species producing it and often track richness poorly. We revise and test an Acoustic Biodiversity Index (ABI) built from species-level detections. Its primary form, ABI_E, is Shannon diversity of detections normalised by the regional species pool expected at the site and season (H / ln S_ref); temporal stability T is reported as a separate component. We first benchmarked four classifiers on a strongly labelled tropical dataset (1,216 calls, 24 classes) with recording-grouped cross-validation. BirdNET embeddings + logistic regression performed best (macro-F1 0.750 +/- 0.029), and random frame-level splits inflated accuracy from 0.41 to 0.70. We then applied BirdNET v2.4 with a location and season filter to recordings from a riverine savanna in the Zambezi Valley, Zimbabwe, and from three habitats at Emirates Park Zoo and Resort, Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates. A stricter post-hoc location filter removed 517 high-confidence detections of 9 implausible species, all at the zoo. After diel-matched rarefaction to equal effort (6 h), the savanna site held 21 species (Hill number 1D = 9.83; ABI_E = 0.38) against 1.3-13 species (ABI_E = 0.03-0.21) at the zoo sites. Across 149 recorded hours, ABI_E correlated strongly with richness (Spearman rho = 0.93), whereas six standard indices did not (best: ACI, rho = 0.48). The stability term was lower at the savanna site (0.39) than at the zoo (0.65-0.67), showing that it penalises the natural diel cycle of bird activity. Species-level indices with explicit false-positive control, a declared regional reference pool and effort standardisation provide a more interpretable biodiversity indicator than energy-based acoustic indices.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: New Lower Bounds for Private PAC Learning
nodes.authors: Prathamesh Dharangutte, Amartya Sanyal
nodes.summary: We study realizable PAC learning under approximate differential privacy, and give a framework for proving lower bounds on its sample complexity. We construct classes with identical VC and Littlestone dimensions but different private sample complexities at common privacy and accuracy parameters, showing that these dimensions do not determine the sample complexity, even for improper learners. To address this we introduce the Independent Class Packing (ICP) parameter, the largest total sample complexity of classes in $\mathcal{G}$ that can be packed independently into a class $\mathcal{H}$, and prove that every $(\varepsilon, δ)$-DP, $(α, β)$-PAC learner for $\mathcal{H}$, possibly improper, uses $Ω\left(\mathrm{ICP}(\mathcal{H}, \mathcal{G})/(α\varepsilon)\right)$ examples. Using this framework we prove tight lower bounds for axis-aligned rectangles, union of intervals and linear subspaces and improved lower bounds for halfspaces and convex polygons. Finally we also show that for product classes, and more generally when the same classes pack into $\mathcal{H}$ and cover its domain so that target labels can be used directly, ICP characterizes private PAC sample complexity up to logarithmic factors.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: Shock Loading Accesses Reaction Pathways beyond Accelerated Thermolysis
nodes.authors: Mingjie Wen, Jiahe Han, Zihan Zhou, Hao Wang, Xueyong Guo, Qingzhao Chu, Dongping Chen
nodes.summary: Thermolysis and shock loading can produce similar major stable products in energetic materials, despite different chemical evolution and reaction pathways. Here, we develop EMFF-MACE, a reactive machine-learning potential for C/H/N/O energetic materials, enabling thermolysis simulations of 20 materials and shock simulations of 10 on a common potential energy surface. Comparisons at matched normalized reaction progress reveal divergent chemical states and local structural environments. Mean reaction-state similarity decreases from 94.0% at 20% progress to 25.9% at trajectory endpoints, while 47.1-92.6% of shock local environments lie outside corresponding material-specific thermolysis reference domains. Structural and reaction-network analyses reveal enhanced intermolecular reorganization and additional association and rearrangement branches under shock loading, despite partially shared early decomposition chemistry. These findings show that loading history influences the structural states and subsequent reaction pathways accessed during decomposition, rather than merely the rate of thermolysis.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: Variance Reduction for Decentralized Stochastic Optimization with Multiple Local Updates
nodes.authors: Jie Liu, Nicola Bastianello, Wenying Xu, Daniel W. C. Ho
nodes.summary: Multiple local updates are widely used in decentralized optimization to enhance communication efficiency, often in conjunction with stochastic gradients when exact gradient computation is costly. However, such algorithms generally converge only to a neighborhood of the optimum, whose size depends on the stepsize and the variance of gradient noise. Variance reduction has been incorporated into ADMM-based methods to achieve exact convergence in expectation, but their stepsizes typically scale inversely with both the square root of the network size and the cube of the number of local updates, leading to slow convergence as the network size or the number of local updates increases. In this paper, we propose a novel primal-dual-based decentralized optimization algorithm that integrates variance reduction with multiple local updates, with a stepsize independent of the network size and inversely proportional to the number of local updates (rather than its cube), thereby enabling significantly larger stepsizes and faster convergence. Moreover, to the best of our knowledge, we establish the first linear convergence guarantee in expectation for decentralized optimization with multiple local updates under stochastic gradients in the strongly convex setting. Beyond the theoretical guarantee, the proposed method exchanges only one variable per round, halving the communication cost compared with gradient-tracking-based methods. Numerical experiments further demonstrate its advantages in convergence speed and accuracy.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: On k-nearest-neighbor regression in metric spaces
nodes.authors: László Györfi, Vladimir G. Pestov, Harro Walk, Roi Weiss
nodes.summary: We study mean squared consistency of k-nearest-neighbor regression for metric space valued features. For a fixed feature distribution mu with atomless distance distributions, we describe how neighbor selection redistributes probability through the density of a uniformly chosen neighbor of an independent query. This gives separate conditions for the approximation error and the conditional response variance, and weakens Stone's domination condition when stronger response moments are available. In particular, when k_n tends to infinity and k_n/n tends to zero, a uniform L2(mu) bound on the selection densities suffices under a finite fourth response moment. We give a corresponding condition in terms of neighborhoods of fixed population mass and recover the Euclidean density bound. Finite global Nagata dimension gives Stone's domination. While sigma-finite Nagata dimensionality is known to ensure universal consistency of k-NN classification in complete separable spaces, we show that this is not the case for mean squared consistency with unbounded responses: we construct a space in this class on which one fixed noiseless response with all finite moments has diverging mean squared error.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: On-Chain Behavioral Signatures for Classifying Centralized Exchange Addresses on Ethereum Using Proof-of-Reserves
nodes.authors: Seongchan Park, Hyunho Jeon, Byungsoo Kang, Gaeun Kim, Minseob So, Seongyong Kim
nodes.summary: Centralized exchanges (CEXs) are key gateways between traditional finance and digital asset markets, yet identifying their blockchain addresses remains challenging. Existing approaches often rely on opaque attribution labels or treat exchanges as secondary classification targets, leaving generalization to unseen exchanges insufficiently examined. This study develops a classification framework using Proof-of-Reserves (PoR) disclosures, with 3,033,857 Ethereum addresses from 15 CEXs and five Non-CEX categories. We derive 58 on-chain behavioral features and evaluate LightGBM against logistic regression (LR) under a leave-one-exchange-out protocol. Across five lookback windows (30-730 days), LightGBM consistently outperformed LR, with macro PR-AUC increasing from 0.6611 to 0.9594 using the selected 17 features, compared with 0.7697 for LR at 730 days. Robustness checks showed comparable performance when feature selection and hyperparameter optimization were repeated across splits and held-out exchanges, while exchange-balanced reweighting improved macro PR-AUC. SHAP analysis and feature-group ablation identified gas behavior, ERC-20 token activity, and internal transactions as key predictive signals in the constructed dataset. These findings support interpretable CEX address screening for blockchain monitoring, while the released feature dataset enables reproducible follow-up research.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: Overcoming the Representational Limitations of Amplitude Encoding for Quantum Neural Networks
nodes.authors: Vincent Gurgul, David Prinz
nodes.summary: Quantum Neural Networks (QNNs) offer a framework for learning functions from classical data, but their expressive power depends critically on how inputs are encoded into quantum states. Angle encoding can require resources that scale with the number of features, whereas amplitude encoding represents $d$ features using only $\mathcal{O}(\log_2 d)$ qubits. This compactness comes at a representational cost: normalization makes conventional amplitude encoding invariant to nonzero real rescaling of the input, up to an unobservable global phase. We show that this invariance induces an exact, architecture-independent restriction on the resulting hypothesis class. No downstream quantum circuit can distinguish inputs differing by nonzero real scaling. We develop a general condition under which deterministic preprocessing can remove this ambiguity and show that nonlinearity alone is insufficient. Based on this analysis, we introduce a fixed nonlinear feature map that provably distinguishes all real inputs under subsequent amplitude encoding, without adding trainable parameters and while retaining logarithmic qubit scaling. We evaluate the resulting QNN on three canonical classification benchmarks and a nonlinear synthetic dataset against conventional amplitude and angle encoding, as well as a classical neural network. Across these tasks, the proposed encoding consistently improves classification accuracy over both quantum encoding baselines by 21$-$44 %. Our results establish normalization-induced scale invariance as a concrete representational bottleneck of amplitude encoding and demonstrate that it can be removed while preserving a compact quantum representation, marking a step toward quantum models capable of capturing arbitrary relationships in classical data.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: Trainable Vector Quantization for Large Language Models
nodes.authors: Anastasiia Prutianova, Alina Bogdanova, Mikhail Shutov, Dmitrii Poimanov, Anatoly Gorkov, Ilia Zharikov
nodes.summary: Vector Quantization (VQ) is a rapidly evolving technique for compressing Large Language Model (LLM) weights, reducing memory usage, and speeding up inference. However, extreme compression deteriorates model performance, which is challenging to recover due to the discrete nature of VQ parameters. Existing methods employ training-free approaches that are limited to layer-wise reconstruction loss minimization. To address this limitation, we propose TVQ, a novel method that leverages straight-through estimation to enable gradient descent-based optimization of vector-quantized LLMs. By reformulating VQ LLM optimization with trainable latent weights, TVQ enables arbitrary objective minimization. We constitute our approach by applying TVQ in a block-wise knowledge distillation paradigm, which balances quality and training efficiency, and propose several practical solutions to accelerate training. In experiments on modern LLMs, we demonstrate that TVQ is compatible with modern VQ schemes. As a result, TVQ achieves state-of-the-art quality in low-bit post-training quantization settings with a modest training budget and straightforward PyTorch implementation. For instance, TVQ achieves near-lossless 2-bit quantization for LLaMA2-70B with only 1% accuracy drop on popular Question-Answering benchmarks.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: ElTab: Elastically Looped Tabular Transformers
nodes.authors: Mieszko Komisarczyk, Saurabh Mathur, Maurice Kraus, Sriraam Natarajan, Kristian Kersting
nodes.summary: Tabular transformer models such as TabPFN achieve strong predictive performance but incur substantial inference costs, making them difficult to deploy in resource-constrained settings. While looped transformers reduce parameter count through weight sharing, they can lose significant predictive power when stopped early. To address this challenge, we introduce the Elastically Looped Tabular Transformer (ElTab), a single model trained to operate across different computational budgets through supervision at randomly sampled early exits. Across 30 OpenML classification datasets, a single ElTab model matches six depth-specific looped models while cutting training cost by more than half, and matches a 12-layer TabPFN-style baseline with 25% fewer inference FLOPs. These results show that elastic-depth training yields a single model that adapts to the deployment budget at hand, offering a favorable trade-off among predictive performance, storage, and computational cost.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: DIFFNAS: Predictor-Free Neural Architecture Search via Diffusion Model and Zero-Cost Evaluation
nodes.authors: Yize Sun, Hanzhang Ma, Zixin Wu, Xuechun Li, Volker Tresp, Yunpu Ma
nodes.summary: Neural Architecture Search (NAS) has advanced the automated design of deep networks, but remains computationally expensive due to reliance on model training or performance predictors. We introduce DIFFNAS, a predictor-free NAS framework that leverages a discrete graph diffusion model guided by zero-cost performance proxies. Unlike prior diffusion-based NAS methods that require learned performance predictors, DIFFNAS conditions the generative process on training-free metrics such as MeCo and SWAP, enabling efficient architecture search with minimal computational overhead. Experiments on NAS-Bench-201 show that DIFFNAS finds the optimal architectures for CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 (94.37% and 73.51%) without a pretrained predictor, while reducing search cost by up to 17.5x compared to DiffusionNAG. On the MobileNetV3 search space, its accuracy is lower than that of DiffusionNAG. These results highlight the promise of diffusion models combined with zero-cost proxies for scalable and effective architecture search.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: Continual Reinforcement Learning Is an Integration Problem
nodes.authors: Nis Meinert, Jakob Gawlikowski, Edward Grant, Max Cyprys, Nathan Schurr, Neil Boston, Alfredo Ibias, Milind Tambe, Janusz Marecki
nodes.summary: This paper presents an opinionated set of ten desiderata intended to inform the design and evaluation of reinforcement-learning agents that learn continually throughout a continuing lifetime. We use these desiderata to examine a representative selection of existing approaches. Progress on individual desiderata is valuable, but the longer-term aim should be to integrate all ten within a single agent. To our knowledge, no published evaluation has yet provided evidence for such an integration. Likewise, the representative benchmarks we review probe different parts of this target, but separate evaluations do not establish that the corresponding properties coexist within one agent throughout a continuing lifetime. As a secondary contribution, we therefore present a compact persistent-world scenario as a playable companion to the desiderata and outline a proposed benchmark that examines a broad range of associated behavioral capabilities together within one such lifetime.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: Exploring Bad Minima in Transfer Learning
nodes.authors: Mina Remeli
nodes.summary: Transfer learning is a highly successful learning paradigm in deep learning which leverages knowledge from one task and applies it to another. Despite its success, the necessary conditions for knowledge transfer are unclear and require further research. In this dissertation, our aim is to understand transferability a little better by answering the following question: Does good generalization on a source task necessarily imply transferability to a related target task? We hypothesize the answer is negative, and attempt to find counterexamples via adversarial attacks on the transfer learning procedure. Over three types of adversarial attacks, our empirical results show a strong relationship between generalization on the source task and transferability. These results do not rule out generalization on the source task as a sufficient condition for successful transfer.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: Backpropagation-free Deep Learning for Time-Series Classification
nodes.authors: Miha Kapš, Blaž Bertalanič, Carolina Fortuna
nodes.summary: Deep neural networks for time series classification (TSC) are trained almost exclusively by error backpropagation, which imposes update locking and the weight-transport problem. Backpropagation-free learning rules such as Direct Feedback Alignment (DFA), Direct Random Target Projection (DRTP), and the diffusion-inspired NoProp relax these constraints but have been evaluated almost exclusively on 2D image benchmarks. We adapt these three learners to univariate TSC with 1D convolutional architectures and present the first systematic study of them across 112 datasets from the UCR time series archive, with one hyperparameter-optimized configuration per method. The optimized learners reach mean F1 scores of 0.76 to 0.79, below ROCKET (0.83) and InceptionTime (0.84). We propose an analysis framework that relates the per-dataset gap to InceptionTime to dataset properties and tests convolutional feature learning by replacing the flatten readout with global average pooling, measured as a difference-in-differences (DD) against a backpropagation control on the identical architecture. Intra-class temporal variability is the dataset property most consistently associated with the gap for all three learners (partial Spearman $ρ$ from $0.28$ to $0.40$). Pooling harms DFA and DRTP more than backpropagation (DD $-0.025$ and $-0.055$), consistent with near-random convolutional features, whereas NoProp tolerates pooling as backpropagation does (DD $+0.013$). Relative to backpropagation on the same architectures, DRTP reduces training floating-point operations (FLOPs) by 33% and trains faster only on series longer than about 700 time steps, DFA yields no computational reduction, and NoProp reduces peak memory by 38% at the cost of 48% longer training.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: What Standard Evaluations Hide About Detectors of Hijacked LLM Agents: Rare Attacks, Unseen Tools and Benchmark Transfer
nodes.authors: Mahmoud Abbasi, Juan M. Núñez V., Amin Shahraki
nodes.summary: Detectors can flag hijacked large language model (LLM) agents from the traces of the tools they call. In the eleven evaluations we audited, attacks or anomalies make up 16% to 86% of the test samples, no evaluation varies that share, and six report no test on data from a second benchmark or source. We ask what such evaluations hide. On the AgentDrift and AgentDojo benchmarks we test trained detectors that read tool identities, behavior, call sequences, step embeddings or text, and a released LLM action monitor, AlignmentCheck, with thresholds fixed on training data or set by the monitor's released decision rule. First, at a 2% attack rate a detector with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.879 reaches a precision of 0.076, and the mix of negatives alone moves that precision between 0.039 and 0.117. Second, as tool coverage, the share of test tool calls whose tool was seen in training, falls, detector rankings cross near 50% coverage and reverse below it, because unseen tools map to inputs that training never reached. Dropout on tool inputs largely removes the reversal. Third, no detector trained on AgentDrift ranks AgentDojo traces better than chance (AUROC 0.47 to 0.52), including one that reaches 0.996 within AgentDojo. The monitor, trained on neither, reaches 0.930, but with its open backbone its released decision rule would still mostly raise false alerts at a 2% attack rate (precision 0.096). We turn these findings into a checklist for evaluating trace detectors.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: Do LLMs Know When They Are Wrong About Molecules? In-Context Property Prediction with Self-Reported Uncertainty
nodes.authors: Matthias Busch, Marius Tacke, Tamadur Albaraghtheh, Sviatlana V. Lamaka, Mikhail L. Zheludkevich, Roland C. Aydin, Christian Feiler, Christian J. Cyron
nodes.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are used in many domains, but molecular property prediction with them is still little explored. In this work we evaluate the capability of 7 frontier LLMs to predict molecular properties together with a self-reported uncertainty from in-context examples, and compare them with classical baselines trained on the same molecules. We use 4 datasets and screen each for contamination of the training data of the LLMs: three are clean, and the fourth, ESOL, is memorised by most of the models and serves as a comparison. On the clean datasets every LLM improves with the context, at 30 examples the most accurate one beats every baseline. The requested reasoning effort changes accuracy little. The self-reported uncertainty ranks the prediction errors weakly, with Spearman rank correlations of up to 0.46, about the level reached by the uncertainties of the baselines. Combining uncertainty and prediction, on lipophilicity the most certain half of the best LLM is the most accurate at small context sizes; on BACE and antiviral, and on lipophilicity at large context sizes, the best LLMs are on par with the best baseline. On the contaminated ESOL dataset the LLMs show no improvement with the context size, as expected for a memorised dataset, and their stated uncertainty is smaller on the molecules whose value they recall.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: Locality-Controlled Out-of-Distribution Guidance for Robust Regulatory DNA Sequence Design
nodes.authors: Dabin Jeong, Marwane Bourdim, Mo Lotfollahi
nodes.summary: Designing regulatory DNA sequences for targeted gene-expression control is an important challenge. Recent approaches frame this task as property-conditioned generation, where diffusion models trained on natural sequences are guided toward high predicted activity through reward-based fine-tuning or sampling-time guidance. We show that single-reward evaluation can obscure reward-hacking behavior. By decomposing evaluation into property, novelty, and plausibility, we identify an empirically underexplored region of the evaluation space in which all three objectives are satisfied, but no existing baseline succeeds. We postulate that this gap arises because prior methods treat guidance primarily as a matter of magnitude. In regulatory DNA, however, sequence grammar is spatially nonuniform: motif positions are sensitive to perturbation, while background regions allow more exploration. We therefore propose LOCOGEN by reformulating guidance as a problem of locality. LOCOGEN learns an invariant motif mask through sequence-level invariance learning to protect motif positions, while applying OOD damping only to background positions. It operates at sampling time on a frozen diffusion backbone, without retraining the backbone. Across HepG2, K562, and SK-N-SH, LOCOGEN reaches this previously underexplored region of the property-novelty-plausibility space. Code is available at https://github.com/Lotfollahi-lab/LocoGen.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: Leveraging Quantum Measurement Randomness for Shot-Efficient Diffusion Models
nodes.authors: Tianhao Guo, Dianxin Zheng, Yuhua Qian, Yaohui Zheng, Yuzhi Yang, Merouane Debbah, Chau Yuen
nodes.summary: In quantum computing, the readout always carries finite-shot sampling noise. Suppressing this noise through repeated measurements raises the cost of a quantum neural network (QNN). Meanwhile, a stochastic diffusion sampler deliberately adds randomness at each reverse (generation) step. This paper turns the measurement noise from a liability into a resource. Specifically, we use the noise quantum measurement produces anyway to replace part of the noise the sampler would otherwise inject. We characterize the measurement error as multinomial sampling noise propagated through a trainable linear readout. To connect the circuit's Born probabilities to the denoising task, we further formulate the diffusion process on a bounded zero-sum hyperplane mapped to the probability simplex. Therefore, we can employ a compensation noise to match the mean and covariance of the shot-noise-free linear update under some minimum shot conditions. Solving this condition for the shot count gives a state-dependent adaptive budget. For the denoising diffusion implicit model (DDIM), this budget increases as the sampler becomes more deterministic. On an eight-dimensional Gaussian mixture, the schedule achieves comparable generation quality with $303$ shots per sample against a high-shot reference of $1.6\times10^{6}$, about $5300\times$ fewer. Latent diffusion experiments on MNIST further validate the proposed mechanism for generation in a learned latent space.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: From fleet trajectories to single-cell promises: hierarchically weighted conformal prediction for battery SOH monitoring
nodes.authors: Xiangyu Liu
nodes.summary: Interval predictions from conformal prediction are usually read as "90% coverage", but on nested battery data that number promises the fleet average, not the individual cell. We measure the gap on 124 public LFP cells under a preregistered three-tier reporting protocol (fleet, batch, cell): pooled coverage looks healthy (0.875-0.906 across splits) while the worst cell is covered 0.1-2% of the time, with exact binomial tests against the nominal level. We then repair part of the gap with a hierarchically weighted conformal engine whose weights consume only side information frozen at prediction time - signature features, batch labels, cycle indices - and never touch residuals. The preregistered repair criterion passes: 10th-percentile cell coverage moves 0.750 to 0.830 (53% of the gap), the worst cell 0.642 to 0.694, with zero deferrals and a flat sensitivity spectrum. What the engine does not repair is localized rather than left open: under protocol drift the frozen weights harm monotonically on the SOH scale (the absolute scale is reported in full), a structural dead end we report instead of tuning away; and repair capacity is bounded by calibration-pool battery diversity, measured on both datasets. On a cross-chemistry external set the calibrated intervals collapse (0.286), while the within-domain skeleton replicates (pooled 0.933, worst cell 0.686). The deliverable is a reporting protocol - three tiers of promise anchored to measured regimes, worst-cell statistics, deferral share - that makes per-cell interval claims auditable before deployment.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: From WSIs to Bulk, Spatial and Single-Cell Transcriptomics via Multi-Scale Graph Neural Networks
nodes.authors: Miguel Andrade, José Almeida, Carlos Santiago, Catarina Barata
nodes.summary: Understanding the spatial distribution of gene expression is key to studying complex diseases like cancer. While Spatial Transcriptomics (ST) and Single-Cell Transcriptomics (scT) provide high-resolution insights, they remain expensive and scarce. In contrast, standard histopathology Whole-Slide Images (WSIs) paired with bulk RNA sequencing are widely available. This work introduces a Multi-Scale Graph Neural Network (GNN) capable of simultaneously predicting bulk, spatial, and single-cell transcriptomics directly from WSIs. By extracting morphological features using a Pathology Foundation Model (PFM) (UNI2-h) and constructing spatial graphs at both patch and cell levels, the model learns the hierarchical relationships within the tissue. The network is trained on a combined dataset of The Cancer Genome Atlas Program (TCGA), Visium, and Xenium samples across lung, kidney, and breast tissues. A hybrid training strategy is employed, leveraging direct supervision alongside weakly supervised consistency losses to ensure predictions align across biological scales. Results show the model accurately predicts gene expression at the slide level and moderately at the patch level (strongest on Xenium), and achieves moderate correlation at the challenging single-cell level. Furthermore, downstream tasks explore the clinical relevance of these predictions, demonstrating their utility in survival analysis, spatial hazard mapping, and tumor classification via molecular signatures.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: A Constructive Orbit-Based Theory of Learnability
nodes.authors: Yunied Puig
nodes.summary: We develop a finite-dimensional orbit framework for constructing data-adapted dictionaries, sparse realizations, and predictive extensions. The method uses wrapped weighted shifts to generate orbit dictionaries and local interpolation maps from independent orbit representatives, turning the learning problem into three explicit tasks: scaffold discovery, sparse realization on the discovered dictionary, and prediction through learned sparse coordinates. We introduce CCDS as the main constructive ingredient: a deviation-controlled sparse realization procedure that recovers MP/OMP-type behavior at the minimal-deviation boundary while allowing feasible interior paths with prescribed residual geometry that is inaccessible to MP/OMP. We prove generic orbit independence, exact block interpolation with norm control, observable bounds on sparse approximation distortion, sparse realization guarantees on selected supports, and fixed-path stability under admissible perturbations of the block interpolants. These results connect sparse approximation, interpolation, and finite-dimensional operator dynamics through the construction and analysis of data-induced orbit dictionaries. Experiments on synthetic geometry, controlled realization tests, and standard classification benchmarks show that selected orbit scaffolds have substantially better matched-rank projection behavior than random orbit or unstructured alternatives, that CCDS attains near-zero realization error at the minimal-deviation boundary, and that predictors trained from the sparse CCDS certificates give competitive performance.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: Co$^2$ODE: Conditionally Coarse-Grained Model Discovery for Rewiring in Biochemical Networks
nodes.authors: Theodore de Pomereu, Fabian Fröhlich
nodes.summary: Biochemical networks propagate the signals that regulate cellular behaviour, and which routes carry them depends on cellular context: a shift in context rewires the network's effective dynamics. Mechanistic simulators are misspecified here because the effective dynamics emerge from an interaction structure that is only partially known. Model discovery instead learns the dynamics from data, but sparse, correlated measurements poorly identify a full network model. What matters is narrower: the portion the context rewires. We introduce conditionally coarse-grained ODEs (Co$^2$ODE), which model that portion as a sparse neural or symbolic ODE: a conditional mask selects the markers carrying the rewiring, and a variational autoencoder compresses the remaining markers into a learnt closure term. On single-cell phosphoproteomic data spanning 30 cancer-relevant overexpressions, Co$^2$ODE compresses a 30-marker panel into a 10-dimensional state while matching the predictive accuracy of a neural ODE fit to the full panel. The closure absorbs what the mask drops, hence the accuracy is insensitive to which markers are kept. Adding a prior score to the loss shifts the selected markers at no cost in fit, indicating the data are not interventional enough to identify the underlying biology.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning
