nodes.title: Which Model for Which Role? Cost-Efficient Pareto Recommendation for LLM Agentic Workflows
nodes.authors: Qian Xie, Wenyue Hua, Yueli He, Sripad Karne, Armaan Agrawal, Nikos Pagonas, Eugene Wu, Kostis Kaffes, Tianyi Peng, Nairen Cao
nodes.summary: LLM agentic workflows increasingly employ different models for specialized roles. Users may prefer different trade-offs between task quality and deployment cost, sometimes also considering latency. Finding good assignments incurs a separate search cost from evaluating multiple candidates. We introduce Cost-Coupled Gittins (CC-Gittins), a multi-objective extension of single-objective cost-aware Gittins search for Pareto recommendation. It exploits the coupling between evaluation and deployment costs: assignments that cost more to deploy also cost more to evaluate. The search alternates between seeking higher quality and lower deployment cost, reusing each evaluation to inform both searches. After each batch, CC-Gittins recommends assignments that are nondominated under uncertainty-adjusted estimates of quality and deployment cost. We evaluate CC-Gittins on eight quality--cost matrices from workflows with two to five roles and up to 1,681 candidate assignments. We also evaluate the method with latency as a third objective. Across the eight benchmarks, CC-Gittins recovers a substantial fraction of the true Pareto frontier at roughly 10% of the exhaustive-evaluation cost, and recovers most of the frontier with few false positives by 30%.
nodes.subject: Computation and Language

nodes.title: The Control Layer Behind Rule-Following Agents Trading Across Market Conditions
nodes.authors: Saad Naja, Nasser Odtallah, Jake Van-Praag, Sarah May
nodes.summary: Trading discipline often fails people. Our study tested whether four AI trading agents followed their strategies and risk rules. Offering traders the evidence and an agent evaluation toolkit to separate luck from following the rules, before giving agents meaningful autonomy or capital. Our study analysed 2,627 closed positions from 12 February to 27 August 2026 across the same asset universe and execution conditions. Most positions were simulated against live prices with a 0.09% round-trip fee; 18% involved real Hyperliquid orders. Each position declared a strategy, stop and target, with a limit of five open positions per agent. The fleet finished net positive after fees. Rule adherence was high across all four agents, including the unprofitable one. Profitability tracked how often agents won relative to their break-even win rates. Institutional-style controls ran by default and contained losses through a 29% market drawdown and recovery, with documented exceptions. The discipline held for all four agents. Agents kept 97.5% of gross loss within declared stops, and typical losses closed at declared levels. Declared risk remained stable after losses and broadly stable across calm and volatile months. Twenty-three of 24 runs respected the position limit; logs identify the exception's size and duration. The same live data produced different results across assigned strategies. The trade-log tests can be rerun from the published trade snapshot; regime tests also require the published Bitcoin prices and regime labels. Section 3.5 specifies the stop-breach tolerance. These trade-level results are not account-level returns or proof of a lasting edge. Our study provides an evaluation toolkit to help traders distinguish rule-following from luck before committing capital. For anyone considering allocating capital to agents to trade, discipline should be the entry test, not the only test.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: CTLite: Lightweight Irregular Multivariate Time Series Forecasting with Reusable Continuous-Time Summaries
nodes.authors: Shusen Ma, Xudong Zuo, Yangchun Xie, Yun-Bo Zhao
nodes.summary: Irregular multivariate time series forecasting (IMTSF) requires capturing temporal dynamics and cross-variable dependencies from sparse, asynchronous observations. Existing methods often rely on learned temporal encoders, coupling historical representation construction with model optimisation and repeatedly processing the same observations. We propose CTLite, a lightweight forecasting framework that decouples historical summarisation from learned prediction. Specifically, a parameter-free continuous-time moment encoder summarises local levels and trends at multiple temporal scales while suppressing poorly supported slope estimates. A compact readout combines damped local extrapolation with a low-rank cross-variable correction that accounts for observation freshness, target availability, and forecast horizon. Since the historical summaries are independent of trainable parameters and forecast queries, they can be reused across optimisation steps and repeated predictions for an unchanged history without altering predictions or parameter gradients. Experiments on four real-world benchmarks show that CTLite achieves the best or second-best mean MSE and MAE among the evaluated methods with only 88-2,537 trainable parameters. Under matched GPU workloads at batch size 32, CTLite reduces inference latency by 18.6-87.3% compared with the latest models, including the cost of historical encoding. Reusing summaries further reduces total runtime by approximately 52% over 16 forecast calls on the same history compared with recomputing the encoder for every call, including the initial encoding cost. The code is at: https://github.com/SSMa913/NICLab-CTLite.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: Learning from Fleet Experience: Collective Experience Learning Across 96 Robots
nodes.authors: Chao Yu, Shu'ang Yu, Hao Lin, Hongzhi Zang, Yuxiang Yan, Chenxi Jiang, Zhen Guo, Chuankang Li, Yihao Chen, Xin Xu, Xu Fu, Jiakai Zhou, Liangzhi Shi, Hongyi Ren, Yiwei Liu, Jing Wu, Yuanqing Wang, Chen Wu, Bo Dai, Chunyu Yang, Hongliang Huang, Shuoyu Yue, Weiqi Yin, Yinuo Chen, Ruihua Chen, Chunyang Zhu, Han Xiao, Yanghao Li, Ruipu Wu, Zhikai Cai, Xiu Chen, Xu Tan, Si Liu, Yuchen Yan, Jialin Zhang, Wen Zeng, Yiming Zhou, Zixiao Huang, Xinlei Chen, Guanghui Ren, Quanlu Zhang, Boxun Li, Maoqing Yao, Yu Wang
nodes.summary: Robot deployment generates experience that can support policy improvement, but continued reliance on expert corrective actions makes learning difficult to scale across growing fleets. We propose learning from fleet experience: using deployed robots' own executions as a source of supervision for further policy improvement. We call this paradigm Collective Experience Learning (CEL), in which robots pool execution experience to update a shared policy that returns to the fleet. Following expert-supervised initialization, we realize CEL through failure-guided experience retrieval fine-tuning (FERT). FERT uses failure contexts to retrieve relevant segments from successful trajectories and prioritizes their recorded actions for supervised updates, without collecting additional expert demonstrations or corrective actions. Operators provide binary episode-outcome labels and environment resets. A fault-tolerant asynchronous training system (FATS) coordinates robot execution, cloud inference and policy optimization despite local interruptions. Across five real-world manipulation tasks, the resulting policies achieve success rates of 93.3-99.2%, evaluated over 120 trials per task on robots excluded from training data collection. With collection time per robot held fixed, larger fleets provide more experience and generally improve performance across the evaluated sizes. On multi-stage phone packaging, learning with 96 robots raises success from 79.2% to 98.3%. These results support CEL as a scalable approach to improving robot policy reliability through experience generated during deployment.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: HP-PnP-Flow: Hybrid Time Scheduling and Projection for Plug-and-Play Image Restoration via Flow Matching
nodes.authors: Yong Li, Xiaojie Wang, Xiaoyan Zhang
nodes.summary: Image restoration is a fundamental inverse problem that seeks to recover high-quality images from degraded observations. Plug-and-Play (PnP) methods provide a flexible framework for integrating pretrained denoisers into iterative reconstruction, whereas flow matching offers an efficient generative modeling approach based on continuous-time ODE dynamics. Very recently, Martin et al.\ (ICLR, 2025) developed a PnP-Flow method, which integrates the PnP framework with flow matching through a time-dependent denoiser constructed from a pretrained flow matching model.By incorporating a different time schedule and an additional pixel-space projection operator, this paper proposes a novel efficient PnP-Flow algorithm (HP-PnP-Flow) that enjoys rigorous convergence guarantees under mild assumptions, without imposing restrictive conditions on iterates required by the aforementioned work. Numerical experiments on CelebA and AFHQ-Cat demonstrate that the newly proposed HP-PnP-Flow algorithm significantly outperforms PnP-Flow on several restoration tasks such as denoising, deblurring, super-resolution, random inpainting, and box inpainting. Notably, our algorithm achieves comparable or better reconstruction quality with substantially fewer iterations, reducing the iteration count from $500$ to $100$ for deblurring and super-resolution on AFHQ-Cat.
nodes.subject: 3D Vision

nodes.title: REFLEX: RNA Ensemble Generation via Flexibility-Calibrated Stochastic Bridge
nodes.authors: Wanli Ma, Tianmeng Hu, Ke Li
nodes.summary: RNA molecules often function through multiple experimentally observed conformational states. A central challenge is to capture ensemble diversity without sacrificing structural fidelity: samples may collapse toward averaged representative structures or drift into unsupported conformational regions. We introduce REFLEX (RNA Ensemble generation calibrated by FLEXibility), a sequence-conditioned generator for RNA backbone-frame ensembles based on a heteroscedastic stochastic bridge on SE(3). During training, experimental B-factors calibrate residue-wise bridge widths, exposing each observed conformer through local perturbation neighborhoods with residue-specific scales while keeping constrained regions sharper. A learned flexibility condition guides the bridge-field network to recover target conformer-specific frames from these calibrated noisy states. At inference, REFLEX uses only the input sequence, requiring no MSA-subsampling heuristics. On a multi-conformer RNA benchmark, REFLEX achieves the best precision-recall trade-off for ensemble coverage across evaluation thresholds, while recovery-stress ablations indicate gains in target-frame recovery under stronger perturbations.
nodes.subject: Generative Search Engines

nodes.title: CIS-Transolver: A Cross-layer Incremental-State Neural Operator for Fine-Scale Automotive Aerodynamic Flow Prediction
nodes.authors: Jianglong Liu, Zhicheng Zhu, Jia Hao, Liangyue Jia, Wenxuan He
nodes.summary: Neural operators offer an efficient data-driven approach to predicting complex automotive aerodynamic flows. However, spectral bias limits their ability to reconstruct fine-scale flow variations around geometric features such as side mirrors and wheel arches. Reliable assessment of local geometric changes therefore requires models that capture fine spatial detail together with global flow interactions. Inspired by iterative refinement and state evolution, we propose CIS-Transolver, a cross-layer incremental-state neural operator that integrates local multiscale information into global flow modeling. The method extracts local feature variations and encodes them as zeroth- to second-order geometric moments. These encodings are combined with information from earlier layers to form a cross-layer memory. Memory-derived corrections enter the value branch of Physics-Attention, allowing local details to inform global physical-state interactions throughout the network. We systematically evaluate CIS-Transolver on three public automotive aerodynamics benchmarks, ShapeNet-Car, AhmedML, and DrivAerNet++, covering surface pressure fields and volumetric pressure and velocity fields. CIS-Transolver achieves the lowest mean relative L2 error among the evaluated methods for all five prediction metrics across the three benchmarks. Relative error reductions average 8.72% compared with the best baseline for each metric. Also achieves the lowest high-frequency spectral errors across all five metrics, with an average relative reduction of 16.06% compared with the best baseline. These results support cross-layer reuse of local information for fine-scale automotive flow prediction.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: Cassette-Editor: An Agent Harness for Editing Video the Way You Do
nodes.authors: Zhixin Zeng, Jiahao Zhong
nodes.summary: Coding agents work in an environment built for them: they read and edit a project, a compiler or a test checks each change automatically and points to the fault, and version control keeps every change in a project that people can review, revert, and continue. Video editing agents lack such an environment; whether an edit is correct shows only in the rendered video, which is costly to inspect and does not point to the decision at fault. Existing systems give the agent either a set of editing operations, which covers only anticipated edits, or a script whose output is a video the user cannot keep editing. We present Cassette-Editor, a complete agent harness for video editing that lets the agent edit the way a person does: knowing what the project allows, seeing what each change affects, and revising from there. It makes the timeline document the agent's action language, in which edits are compositions of typed changes rather than separate tools. A schema check and a rulebook shared with manual editing define what the project allows. An accepted patch commits as one step of the history the user also edits; a rejected one leaves the project unchanged, with each problem located and repair options listed for the next attempt. Reads map source analysis to the frames of the current edit, so the agent can tell what the edit now shows. A parity evaluation shows that every manual action the editor registers, on its test fixtures, can be expressed as an agent patch that reaches the same independently specified document. In a preliminary case study of consecutive revisions to a long documentary rough cut, Cassette-Editor completed more of the judged requests than Codex CLI, which worked from media files without the project, with the same model at similar cost; with a stronger model, under which both completed every request, it used fewer tokens and less time per delivery.
nodes.subject: Multimedia

nodes.title: A latent control model for realistic rodent motion
nodes.authors: Aidan Sirbu, Charles Y. Zhang, Yuanjia Yang, Bence P. Ölveczky, Talmo D. Pereira, Blake A. Richards
nodes.summary: The development of embodied models of animal behavior is a major goal of the neuro-AI community. Embodied models will enhance our ability to make direct comparisons between biological and artificial agents. To make such comparisons effective, though, we need embodied models that actually move like animals. Previous work has developed virtual animal bodies and techniques for training realistic motion through imitation. However, to date, there is no system for embodied animal modeling that produces natural movements both during trained goal-directed behavior, and during exploration driven by random generation. Here, we introduce Simulated Control via Augmented Motor Priors for Embodied Reinforcement learning (SCAMPER), a system for training an embodied virtual rat model, enabling natural movements during both goal-directed behavior and random exploration. SCAMPER uses a variational architecture with two distinct priors, a motion prior for control and a behavior prior for exploration. We show that combining both of these priors allows SCAMPER to generate realistic behavior during exploration and exploit the task structure effectively. SCAMPER can also learn from sparse rewards as a result of the diverse movements induced by the behavior prior, allowing the system to model realistic sparse-reward tasks from experimental neuroscience. Altogether, SCAMPER provides the neuro-AI community with an effective new system for training embodied models of rodents on realistic tasks.
nodes.subject: Embodied Intelligence

nodes.title: Cassette-Editor: An Agent Harness for Editing Video the Way You Do
nodes.authors: Zhixin Zeng, Jiahao Zhong
nodes.summary: Coding agents work in an environment built for them: a compiler or a test checks each change and points to the fault, and version control keeps every change in a project people can continue. Video editing agents lack one: an edit's correctness shows only in the costly rendered video, which does not point to the decision at fault, and existing systems offer either editing operations that cover only anticipated edits or a script whose output is a video the user cannot keep editing. We present Cassette-Editor, a complete agent harness for video editing that lets the agent edit the way a person does: knowing what the project allows, seeing what each change affects, and revising from there. The agent writes patches of typed changes to the editor's timeline document. A schema check and a rulebook shared with manual editing check each patch before it commits; a rejected patch leaves the project unchanged and returns each problem located with repair options, and an accepted one becomes a step of the history the user also edits. Reads map source analysis to the frames of the current edit. Because manual gestures are writes in the same language, folded by the same executor and rulebook, the agent can express every change a manual edit makes to the project. On 31 editing requests with the model held fixed, the complete harness passed 89% of trials against 47% for the same model with ten basic editing operations and without the rulebook, at less than half the agent time and cost per successful request; the loss fell on requests at rule boundaries, composite edits, and undo, not on finding content.
nodes.subject: Generative Recommendation Systems

nodes.title: EpiLens: Lightweight RAG for Epidemiological Knowledge Acquisition
nodes.authors: Vincenzo Perri, Ciro Cattuto, Daniela Paolotti
nodes.summary: To prepare for future outbreaks, researchers need to know what studies have been done and what data they use. Mapping a large literature by hand is slow, while large language models alone can misstate or conflate sources. We present EpiLens, a lightweight, open-source retrieval-augmented generation package that applies a fixed retrieval template and output schema to every paper in a corpus and links outputs to source passages. We build a corpus of 2,297 papers from the sources of a multi-pathogen parameter study and evaluate EpiLens's paper-classification workflow against 214 manually labelled papers. Run locally with an open-weight model, so that licensed full texts never leave our hardware, the classifier is comparable to supervised baselines trained on the manual labels, and ahead of them on geography, despite the lack of task-specific training data. The study's early extraction sheets cite published sources for 327 estimates. We link each estimate to a cited document or to corpus studies included by a review. Then, we use the classifier's labels to compare the papers associated with different parameters and pathogens. EpiLens labels more papers linked to reproduction numbers than fatality risks as model-based (53% versus 15%, compared with 62% versus 24% in the manual labels). The gap is consistent with the frequent use of transmission models to estimate reproduction numbers and largely persists within pathogens.
nodes.subject: Computation and Language

nodes.title: RefCraft: Benchmarking Visual-Reference-Conditioned Agentic Generation through Web Development
nodes.authors: Yuchi Wang, Rongyao Fang, Weihao Yu, Xilin Wei, Tiancheng Gu, Dingkang Yang, Hang Zhang, Dayiheng Liu, Hongsheng Li, Shuai Bai
nodes.summary: Beyond basic tool use and coding skills, effectively incorporating visual references into agentic generation is equally essential for applying AI agents to real-world productivity tasks. We study this crucial capability through webpage development, a practical and readily evaluable setting in which existing benchmarks remain largely idealized: they typically focus on reconstructing visual targets or generating webpages from textual instructions alone, overlooking the more common workflow of developing from visual examples. Specifically, we introduce RefCraft, a benchmark comprising 300 realistic multimodal webpage-development tasks that combine natural-language instructions with screenshots from one to five reference webpages. Agents must selectively interpret and utilize these references while rendering, visually inspecting, and iteratively refining their outputs. We evaluate the resulting open-ended artifacts using independently verifiable keypoints and complementary programmatic and VLM judges. Across nine frontier (M)LLMs, the strongest system achieves an overall score of only 52.12 out of 100, revealing that visual-reference-conditioned agentic generation remains a substantial challenge for current models in practical webpage-development settings.
nodes.subject: 3D Vision

nodes.title: Learn the Task, Not the Schedule: Reducing Spurious Cross-Arm Coupling in Bimanual Imitation Learning
nodes.authors: Shuyuan Hu, Deng-Ke Wu, Yifan Jin, Qianhang Luo, Mingchen Ju, Kai Ye, Bo Zhao
nodes.summary: A bimanual demonstration specifies both what the robot should do and one particular schedule for when each arm should act. Standard imitation learning does not distinguish task-required cross-arm constraints from incidental scheduling choices, and may therefore exploit opposite-arm progress as a shortcut cue, creating spurious cross-arm coupling even where relative timing is irrelevant for the current task phase. We introduce Constraint-preserving Temporal Recombination (CTR), a training-time data intervention that preserves recorded arm-local sensorimotor content while retiming the corresponding segments to realize admissible schedules that preserve task-required cross-arm constraints. We use CTR to train Diffusion Policy, Action Chunking with Transformers, and $π_{0.5}$, and evaluate them on four simulated and four real-robot tasks. Across six real-robot bimanual progress-state initializations, CTR raises worst-state success from 56% for the strongest non-CTR schedule mixture to 76%. With $π_{0.5}$ on an Independent task, a 4 s pause transfers 2.56 s of delay to the opposite arm under the Concurrent schedule distribution, but only 0.25 s with CTR. On real robots, CTR violates task constraints in only 0--4% of trials, versus 36--98% for narrow-schedule baselines. Code will be released at https://github.com/MINT-SJTU/CTR.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: HP-PnP-Flow: Hybrid Time Scheduling and Projection for Plug-and-Play Image Restoration via Flow Matching
nodes.authors: Yong Li, Xiaojie Wang, Xiaoyan Zhang
nodes.summary: Image restoration is a fundamental inverse problem that seeks to recover high-quality images from degraded observations. Plug-and-Play (PnP) methods provide a flexible framework for integrating pretrained denoisers into iterative reconstruction, whereas flow matching offers an efficient generative modeling approach based on continuous-time ODE dynamics. Very recently, Martin et al. (ICLR, 2025) developed a PnP-Flow method, which integrates the PnP framework with flow matching through a time-dependent denoiser constructed from a pretrained flow matching model. By incorporating a different time schedule and an additional pixel-space projection operator, this paper proposes a novel efficient PnP-Flow algorithm (HP-PnP-Flow) that enjoys rigorous convergence guarantees under mild assumptions, without imposing restrictive conditions on iterates required by the aforementioned work. Numerical experiments on CelebA and AFHQ-Cat demonstrate that the newly proposed HP-PnP-Flow algorithm significantly outperforms PnP-Flow on several restoration tasks such as denoising, deblurring, super-resolution, random inpainting, and box inpainting. Notably, our algorithm achieves comparable or better reconstruction quality with substantially fewer iterations, reducing the iteration count from $500$ to $100$ for deblurring and super-resolution on AFHQ-Cat.
nodes.subject: 3D Vision

nodes.title: TimesJev: Thinking Fast on Time Series with System 1 Sufficiency
nodes.authors: Chenghao Liu, Wei Fan, Jindong Han, Dongjie Wang, Aniket Mahanti, Pengyang Wang, Hao Liu
nodes.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have recently shown strong potential for time series reasoning, while models that reason over time series are usually with long chains of thought. However, this process often consumes thousands of tokens, directly leading to substantial latency during inference. In contrast, System 1 models such as Jev make decisions instantly and can naturally be an alternative, but raw time series are not compatible with the embedding space of these models, thus hindering the reasoning performance, especially when input series contain thousands of numeric points. In this paper, we make a very early attempt to propose a time series System 1 model, namely TimesJev. Specifically, we first formalize System 1 sufficiency in time series reasoning, which motivates a compressed representation for time series with key frequency patterns preserved. To construct this representation, we derive a dimension reduction objective that combines (i) a sufficiency divergence that measures the core information lost during compression, and (ii) a realizability divergence that quantifies the incompatibility of the System 1 model to the optimal prediction given this representation. We optimize this objective by learning time series compression with a gating mechanism for sufficiency, and then aligning the selected representation with the embedding space for realizability. Finally, experiments on 13 datasets demonstrate that TimesJev outperforms reasoning models by over 62% with 62.9% less inference time than their fine-tuned versions on average.
nodes.subject: Generative Recommendation Systems

nodes.title: Physiology-Aware Graph Attention for Early Ventricular Reentry Prediction
nodes.authors: Ma{ë}lis Morier, Jairo Rodr{í}guez Padilla, Mihaela Pop, Patrick Gallinari, Maxime Sermesant
nodes.summary: Sudden cardiac death mostly originates from post-infarct ventricular tachycardia. This reentry is sustained by propagation around scar tissue, but its risk remains difficult to predict from infarct imaging alone. While in silico induction studies can reveal these mechanisms, exploring many substrates and pacing locations remains computationally expensive. We propose a graph attention classifier for early prediction of sustained ventricular reentry from simulated cardiac electrophysiology. Each simulation is represented as a graph with early nodal voltage samples and edge attributes encoding geometry, stimulation frequency, tissue labels, amplitude, and diastolic interval. These descriptors are computed only from the first two paced activations, before sustained reentry is observed. On a balanced independent test set of 1000 simulations, the classifier achieves 94.6% accuracy, 95.4% sensitivity, 93.8% specificity, 94.6% F1-score, 0.987 ROC-AUC, and 0.985 PR-AUC. Ablation experiments show that diastolic interval is the most critical descriptor. Qualitative attention inspection suggests that different heads focus on border-zone, stimulation location, and early propagation path. These results support graph attention as a fast early-prediction approach for large-scale in silico ventricular reentry studies.
nodes.subject: Generative POI Search and Recommendation

nodes.title: Cassette-Editor: Shared Timeline Semantics for Human and Agent Editing
nodes.authors: Zhixin Zeng, Jiahao Zhong
nodes.summary: Video editing involves tedious manual manipulation across interconnected timeline tracks, motivating automated agents that offload routine work while keeping the project directly revisable by humans. Fixed operation catalogs limit expressiveness, while even a basic trim requires coordinated updates across later clips, attached titles, and transitions. We present Cassette-Editor, an agent harness that unifies manual user gestures and automated agent patches within a shared editing environment. The shared action language expresses the editor's manual content changes, and a common history records committed edits for undo and manual refinement. When the model selects an edit, a state executor automatically derives its downstream consequences, such as shifting later clips and attached titles after a trim, while a validation rulebook enforces structural invariants and returns localized diagnostics for automated repair. To keep the agent grounded as the project evolves, dynamic read operations map transcripts and shot descriptions onto the current timeline. Evaluated with GPT-6 Luna, the full harness passed the scored request checks in 92/93 trials across 31 authored requests on two interview documentaries, compared with 48/93 for an internal basic-tools baseline. In ablations, disabling the consequences derived by the executor reduced passed trials from 230/232 to 199/232 on edits with dependent timeline elements, while ablating rulebook validation and repair lowered passed trials from 46/48 to 10/48 on requests operating near structural validity boundaries. Evaluating the complete system on 50 TVSum videos further demonstrated greater agreement with human annotations than a general agent using the same model (F1 23.8 vs. 20.1).
nodes.subject: Multimedia

nodes.title: Latent Projection for Latent Planning
nodes.authors: Yoo Sung Jang, Michael Ryoo
nodes.summary: Latent world models let an agent plan in latent space. The planner searches for an action sequence that minimizes a cost, and that cost is often the $\ell_2$ distance between the predicted terminal latent and the goal latent. The latent, however, is partly noise: the regularizer that prevents collapse during world model training promotes variance in the directions carrying no signal. We show that the same regularizer also supplies the structure to prune that noise in the latent. SIGReg drives the latent marginal to a standard Gaussian at every step, and assuming further that the latent sequence is a Gauss-Markov process, the transition is linear with its covariance pinned by the map itself, $z' \mid z \sim N(Az,\, I - AA^\top)$. Fitting the state dynamics $A$ therefore yields the covariance at no additional cost, and in its eigenbasis each latent direction carries its own uncertainty. Furthermore, constraining $A$ to be a normal matrix fixes that basis across timesteps, so one eigenbasis measures the uncertainty over an arbitrary number of steps and serves as a stable basis to compute the planning cost on. We then restrict the $\ell_2$ cost to the $k$-dimensional subspace the state dynamics carry forward with the least uncertainty. The correction is post hoc: the encoder, the predictor, the rollout, and the planner are all left untouched, and only a single constrained matrix, $A$, is fit. We evaluate across six environments and show large gains on the 2D navigation tasks, TwoRoom and PointMaze, raising success rate over the plain $\ell_2$ cost by up to $+54.7$ points under a harder planning setting. Code is available at https://github.com/yjang43/lp2.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: Computation, Not Memory: Chain-of-Thought and State Tracking in LLM Agents
nodes.authors: Pedram Mouseli, Massieh Moayedi
nodes.summary: Language-model agents often reason before they act, and the value of monitoring that reasoning depends on how it relates to their actions. We ask how an agent's actions depend on its reasoning when the correct action depends on a changing state. In a small file-system task, background events announce which file's lock has been toggled but not its new value. The agent therefore has to reconstruct the current locks from its history before it can move files safely. With Qwen3-8B and Qwen3.5-9B, we separate two roles of reasoning: generating it before each action, and retaining earlier reasoning in the prompt. Most of the reduction in lock-violating commands comes from reasoning written at the moment of action. Retaining earlier reasoning adds little when the agent also reasons at each step, but it helps an agent that does not reason, and it helps in longer episodes. Retained notes have a limit: when a later event makes a note wrong, an agent without current reasoning responds little, while current reasoning makes the action follow the event. The benefit depends on what the reasoning says. Filler text, reasoning written for another history and an accurate table of the state do not reproduce it. When we give the agent reasoning written for a history that differs in one lock value, the agent acts on that reasoning even against its own history. For Qwen3-8B, this holds also when that value has since been toggled. Without reasoning, state readouts are less reliable after toggles, and Qwen3-8B's answers about the state favor the outdated value. The state answer and the action also depend on different parts of the prompt. In this setting, the benefit of reasoning for rule-following comes mainly from generating it at each step, where it makes the action respond to later events. The state that can be read out without reasoning is a limited guide to how the agent acts.
nodes.subject: Spatial Agents

nodes.title: MemT-1.0: Towards Memory-Native Evolution
nodes.authors: Zhiyu Li, Zeyu Zhang, Linyun Liu, Yiwei Bu, Chenyang Xi, Xichong Zhang, Yi Yu, Yu Yu, Zhichen Liu, Yuxiao Yi, Chunyu Li, Haoran Liu, Zhenkai Ding, Le Zhou, Juncheng Zhang, Boyu Chen, Zehao Lin, Guorui Li, Renyu Fu, Ji Li, Youyang Xia, Jiajun Shen, Harvey Li, Jinsong Zhou, Helan Hu, Tong Shen, Tianxiao Xu, Chenye Han, Weijie Li, Zhongquan Zhou, Hongming Xu, Yuekeng Li, Erenkai Zhu, Peng Yu, Wenhao Li, Jingyi Kang, Xixuan Hao, Xuzhou Zhu, Can Chen, Jiawei Liu, Chen Jiang, Tao Jiang, Fangwei Xiang, Zepeng Yao, Kai Chen, Guang Yang, Mingfei Lu, Chunhui Li, Zhengxuan Jiang, Bo Tang, Shiyu Zhan, Yihang Sun, Jie Chu, Wenjun Xiong, Zhenxiang Hua, Chen Lin, Detong Su, Dongyu Deng, Qiuping Ding, Guofeng Ding, Si Chen, Guohua Wen, Xu Chen, Zhi-Qin John Xu, Ying-Cong Chen, Ningyu Zhang, Haofen Wang, Muning Wen, Haotian Chen, Wentao Zhang, Xuanhe Zhou, Rita Zhang, Junchi Yan, Feiyu Xiong
nodes.summary: Memory-native evolution requires making memory an intrinsic capability of foundation models, enabling them to continuously accumulate and utilize information. To this end, we introduce MemT-1.0, a new architecture of memory foundation models that internalize memory as part of model computation. Building on Metis, MemT-1.0 employs Gated DeltaNet-2 with a stable token-level memory update mechanism within each turn. We further introduce Mixture-of-Storage to scale native memory capacity. Following a deliberate backbone preparation, we develop a two-stage training pipeline consisting of continued pre-training and post-training, supported by 34B tokens of training data and efficient training and inference infrastructure. We release a model family comprising MemT-1.0-Nano, MemT-1.0-Flash, and MemT-1.0-Pro, and conduct a comprehensive evaluation of memory and general capabilities. The results show that they outperform the parametric memory baselines on average and remain competitive with retrieval-augmented methods, while largely preserving general capabilities. At a history length of 128K tokens, MemT-1.0-Nano achieves approximately $1.86\times$ end-to-end inference speedup and a $66\times$ reduction in persistent storage relative to full context KV cache. By internalizing retrieved procedural experience, MemT-1.0 improves task success on agentic tasks, providing a practical step toward memory-native evolution.
nodes.subject: Computation and Language

nodes.title: RoboValue: A Fine-Grained Sim-and-Real Benchmark for Unified Evaluation of Robotic Value Models
nodes.authors: Shengbang Liu, Zhengye Du, Zhilong Wan, Honghao Su, Chenxiang Xia, Chang Ge, Jinyang Xiao, Nan Wang, Zhipeng Hu, Huining Yuan, Shu'ang Yu, Yue Chen, Tianxing Chen, Chuankang Li, Maoqing Yao, Wenbo Ding, Yu Wang, Guanghui Ren, Chao Yu
nodes.summary: Robotic value models assess task execution from visual observations and instructions, providing feedback on execution quality and progress toward the task goal. However, existing evaluations cover only selected aspects of execution understanding, leaving the reliability of value feedback insufficiently tested. We introduce RoboValue, a fine-grained sim-and-real benchmark for unified evaluation of robotic value models. Its framework evaluates four complementary capability dimensions through shared interfaces: task-state understanding, temporal progress monitoring, failure and recovery reasoning, and value consistency. Diagnostic trajectories and instruction variations test whether value judgments accurately reflect task requirements and changes throughout execution. RoboValue-Dataset covers 15 simulation and 20 real-world manipulation tasks, providing expert demonstrations for training and annotated trajectories for fine-grained evaluation. We evaluate representative robotic value models and general-purpose multimodal models in zero-shot and one-shot settings under standard conditions and separate shifts in robot embodiment and environment. Models trained to grade partial outcomes and individual task steps exhibit strong fine-grained grounding, while reasoning over observation histories supports tracking of accumulated task effects. Strong forward-progress and memory scores can nevertheless coexist with poor responses to task regression. Even models with strong grounding and progress estimates struggle to recognize effective recovery and to give consistent feedback within and across valid executions. These findings identify concrete targets for value supervision, while the dataset and public leaderboard support continued assessment of feedback reliability. The website is available at https://robovalue-benchmark.github.io/.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: PhysSkin++: Generalizable Self-Supervised Neural Skinning for Real-Time Interactive Physics-Based Animation
nodes.authors: Yuanhang Lei, Baofei Liu, Xingxuan Li, Tao Cheng, Zixuan Wang, Boming Zhao, Yujun Shen, Siyuan Huang, Ruizhen Hu, Peter Yichen Chen, Hujun Bao, Zhaopeng Cui
nodes.summary: Generalizing real-time physics-based animation across diverse 3D shapes and spatial discretizations remains challenging. In this paper, we introduce PhysSkin++, a physics-informed framework that learns continuous neural skinning fields from static geometries to construct compact deformation subspaces. Specifically, we propose a Neural Skinning Fields Autoencoder that predicts shape-dependent deformation subspaces without per-object network training. To learn these subspaces without simulation trajectories, we develop a Physics-Informed Self-Supervised Learning strategy that combines skinning-field normalization with conflict-aware gradient correction, stabilizing joint optimization under physical and orthogonality constraints. The learned representation supports efficient reduced dynamics with user control and contact interactions, together with direct animation binding to meshes, point clouds, and 3D Gaussians. For prescribed rig animation, we further introduce a self-supervised complementarity objective to learn complementary elastic responses without enforcing complementarity constraints at runtime. Experiments demonstrate cross-shape generalization of the learned skinning fields, real-time reduced simulation, and applications to controllable, collision-aware, and rig-complementary animation.
nodes.subject: 3D Vision

nodes.title: Vector-Quantized World Model: Latent Feedback Motion Planning for Robot Manipulation
nodes.authors: Xuezhou Xu, Chung-Pang Wang, Zhenzhen Li, Benjamin Riviere
nodes.summary: Visual world models have shown strong potential for robot planning, yet long-horizon manipulation remains challenging due to compounding prediction errors, large search complexity, and latent plans that the low-level controller cannot reliably reach. In this work, we introduce Vector-Quantized World Model (VQ-WM), a latent feedback motion planning framework that integrates discrete long-horizon search with continuous visual feedback control: a discrete latent predictor models transitions between vector-quantized latent states, allowing the planner to look far ahead and find a shortest path to the goal through discrete search and a continuous learned controller sequentially reaches the planned states through visual feedback, correcting deviations to mitigate compounding errors. Whereas most vector quantization uses Euclidean distance, we use a novel estimator of the first-passage-time as a quasi-metric, which aligns the planning abstraction with the controller's capabilities. We evaluate on the physical robot manipulation of the Tower of Hanoi puzzle: whereas existing state-of-the-art foundation models (VLAs, WAMs) only succeed when the solution trace in their training dataset, our method achieves 100\% success rate with only short-play data, demonstrate its ability to compose long-horizon solutions beyond the short demonstrated trajectories and execute them reliably. Our solution also outperforms strongest world-models by 13.3--85.3 percentage points on simulation benchmarks spanning manipulation and locomotion, demonstrating consistent progress and new capabilities.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: A 3D-Driven Framework for Moving-Camera Perspective-to-360° Video Generation
nodes.authors: Michael Wakeham, Mrinmoy Kumar Das, Wenqi Wang, Ayush Tewari, Boqing Gong, Deepti Ghadiyaram
nodes.summary: Turning a moving-camera perspective video into a 360° video means generating content outside the input frame under several constraints: observations revealed over time must be preserved, unseen regions plausibly completed, and the resulting scene kept consistent as the camera viewpoint changes. Existing methods assign these different requirements to a single conditional video model, requiring them to be jointly learned from panoramic video data. We instead present a modular, 3D-driven framework that distributes these three responsibilities across specialized components, all connected through a shared scene representation. Input observations are reconstructed explicitly in 3D, while a pretrained panoramic image model completes unobserved content from a selected panoramic render. This generated content is lifted into the shared 3D scene, where it remains spatially anchored across camera viewpoints. Without requiring any additional panoramic-video training, our framework achieves state-of-the-art input-view fidelity, perceptual quality, and geometric consistency on a static-scene subset of the Argus evaluation set. These results support our decomposed, 3D-driven formulation as a promising alternative to direct video generation in this setting.
nodes.subject: 3D Vision

nodes.title: Learning Lane-Structured Conditioning Fields for Online HD Mapping
nodes.authors: Andrea Bertogalli, Anthony Dell'Eva, Marcello Ceresini, Federico Pirazzoli, Lorenzo Cipelli, Filippo D'Addeo, Nicola Marinello, Massimo Bertozzi
nodes.summary: High-definition maps provide critical structural information for downstream autonomous driving tasks. Recent methods increasingly rely on external priors to improve prediction accuracy and robustness. Yet, existing prior representations expose a trade-off: dense rasters are easy to integrate but ignore certain map geometric properties, while sparse vectors preserve geometric structure but require dedicated encoders and are difficult to plug into existing architectures. Moreover, external priors can be inaccurate, costly to acquire, or difficult to maintain, motivating a structural representation that can provide geometric guidance while remaining learnable and broadly applicable. We address this limitation with the Lane Field, a dense BEV-aligned geometric representation that encodes local lane structure at each spatial location and can be either predicted from onboard observations or constructed from external map priors. Building on this representation, we introduce a plug-and-play framework that enhances online HD mapping through two complementary mechanisms: BEV feature modulation, which injects lane-structured cues into latent BEV features, and deformable attention guidance, which steers query sampling toward the underlying lane geometry. We primarily evaluate our method on OpenLane-V2, showing that conditioning BEV features and guiding deformable attention with local lane geometry enables our framework to consistently improve existing methods and achieve state-of-the-art performance on lane segment perception. Project page: https://andberto.github.io/LaneField/
nodes.subject: End-to-End AD

nodes.title: P2N: Reusing Deep Representations for Greater Effective Depth
nodes.authors: Yiqin Hao, Boyi Zeng, Zitong Wang, He Li, Shixiang Song, Feichen Song, Yifan Liu, Ran Tao, Bryan Dai, Zhouhan Lin
nodes.summary: Mathematical problem solving and autonomous agents are increasingly important applications of language models, demanding stronger reasoning capabilities. Computational depth is a key resource for such reasoning, but adding model layers increases both training and inference costs, while test-time scaling incurs substantial additional inference computation. We introduce P2N (Previous to Next), which reuses the previous token's deep representations, already available during generation, to increase effective computational depth with negligible decoding overhead. Specifically, P2N adds the previous token's deep hidden state to the current token's shallow representation, allowing subsequent layers to build on previously completed deep computation. This recurrence extends effective computational depth across tokens, while introducing only a single vector addition per decoding step. We train the recurrence using parallel Jacobi updates restricted to a middle-layer core. Experiments with Qwen-style models show that, at 1.5B parameters, P2N improves GSM8K accuracy by over 10 percentage points under both zero-shot and few-shot prompting, with nearly unchanged decoding latency. The benefits also extend to language modeling and average performance on general downstream benchmarks. on general downstream benchmarks.

nodes.title: Toward Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Enterprise Retail Workflows over Heterogeneous Data Sources
nodes.authors: Jeonghwan Choi, Jibin Hwang, Hayoon Park, Hyeonjae Cheon, Hwanjun Song
nodes.summary: Enterprise retail workflows require agents to chain evidence across heterogeneous sources, from structured product and order records to unstructured inquiries and reviews, yet existing agentic RAG benchmarks rarely capture this challenge. To enable controlled evaluation of such workflows, we introduce RetailBridge, a compositional retail benchmark built from persona-driven simulations. Its questions are constructed by linking entities and intermediate answers across heterogeneous sources, requiring agents to identify the relevant sources, carry evidence between them, and produce a grounded answer. To systematically evaluate LLMs on these retail workflows, we develop RetailRAG, a retail-aware framework equipped with auto-schema briefing, source-routed plan chaining, and diagnostic plan revision. RetailRAG consistently outperforms existing agentic RAG baselines across all evaluation axes, serving as a strong reference system for assessing LLM agents on retail workflows. On RetailBridge, evaluating ten LLM backbones with RetailRAG reveals multi-source chaining as the dominant bottleneck across providers and model scales, suggesting that reliable retail agents require explicit cross-source orchestration rather than scaling alone. Code and data are publicly available at https://github.com/DISL-Lab/RetailBridge.
