nodes.title: PFM-HR: Pose Flow Matching for Humanoid Robots
nodes.authors: Yukang Gao, Yi Gu, Yangchen Zhou, Xingyu Chen, Zhaorui Wang, Fanghai Zhang, Hanyang Cao, Zhengyang Shen, Ji Ma, Runhan Zhang, Lei Han, Renjing Xu
nodes.summary: Motion priors improve reinforcement learning for physics-based humanoid tracking, but temporal priors require ordered motion clips, while pose priors provide limited guidance for policy-induced pose transitions. We present Pose Flow Matching for Humanoid Robots (PFM-HR), a reusable flow matching prior trained directly on large scale unordered pose data. PFM-HR introduces the Pose Geometry Score (PGS), which quantifies how joint coordinate changes during rollouts align with the local geometry of pose variation captured by the prior. Using PGS to modulate the tracking reward guides policy exploration toward structured pose changes while keeping the prior frozen across tracking tasks. Experiments demonstrate that PFM-HR improves both single motion and general motion tracking, especially for highly dynamic motions.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: Morphology-Aware Implicit Super-Resolution Network for Pathological Images
nodes.authors: Jiaming Liang, QiHui Han, Haolin Chen, Chengxin Ye, Jiawen Liu, Jiazhou Chen, Xiaoqi Sheng, Hongmin Cai
nodes.summary: Accurate diagnosis in Digital Pathology (DP) relies on high-resolution whole-slide images, yet clinical deployment is often limited by hardware costs. Super-Resolution (SR) offers a promising alternative by computationally enhancing low-resolution acquisitions. However, existing SR methods frequently struggle to preserve fine-grained cellular morphology, leading to texture oversmoothing and blurred structural boundaries under complex tissue variability. To address this issue, we propose Morph-ISR, a morphology-aware implicit super-resolution framework for DP that restores diagnostically relevant details with sub-pixel precision. Morph-ISR reformulates SR as a continuous coordinate-based reconstruction problem and integrates an Implicit Position-aware Kernel Generator (IPKG) to adaptively model spatially varying tissue morphology. To further enhance structural fidelity, a Morphological Fidelity Prior (MFP) is introduced, leveraging semantic guidance from a pre-trained cell segmentation network to enforce boundary-preserving and region-aware reconstruction, thereby improving the representation of critical cellular boundaries and nuclear textures. Experiments on TCGA and SurGen datasets show that Morph-ISR achieves the best LPIPS and ST-LPIPS among the evaluated methods, reducing them by up to 38.37% and 39.55%, respectively, over the second-best methods while maintaining strong PSNR and SSIM. These results demonstrate superior preservation of diagnostically relevant cellular boundaries and nuclear textures, while compact parameterization and high throughput support efficient edge deployment. Code and trained models will be released upon publication.
nodes.subject: 3D Vision

nodes.title: An ECG foundation model for zero-shot transfer from hospital to point-of-care devices
nodes.authors: Edoardo Coppola, Stefano Fiorini, Pietro Liò, Mattia Savardi, Alberto Signoroni
nodes.summary: Electrocardiogram (ECG) recording is moving from hospitals to point-of-care devices that record one or two leads, where public labelled data is too scarce to build foundation models (FMs) as for 12-lead ECGs. Whether existing 12-lead FMs transfer to these devices without retraining is unknown. We show that seven published FMs reach a zero-shot AUROC of 41-81% on two real point-of-care datasets and, when reduced to one or two leads, lose 12-35 AUROC points on average and gain 0.15-0.23 in mean absolute error across 29 benchmarks covering 1,673 clinical targets. We present RELAY, a 7-million-parameter FM that represents ECGs as graphs of segments from whichever leads are recorded, without filling missing ones or knowing their identities. Pretrained on 9.2 million 12-lead ECGs, RELAY is competitive with 12 leads, ranks first on both point-of-care datasets (AUROC 87.6% and 81.5%) and on 26 and 22 of 29 benchmarks with one and two random leads, and keeps the most informative operating point when 12-lead thresholds are applied to device recordings. Matched ablations show that omitting absent leads, rather than filling them, reduces what RELAY loses in transfer. ECG FMs should therefore be judged across all the acquisition settings, not on 12-lead benchmarks alone.
nodes.subject: Generative POI Search and Recommendation

nodes.title: Projection-Retraction MPPI: Exact Command-Space Constraint-Manifold Control for Manipulators
nodes.authors: Seulchan Lee, Leesai Park, Minhyeong Kang, Sanghyun Kim
nodes.summary: Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) control is widely used in manipulation for its gradient-free, parallel handling of non-convex costs. Manipulation tasks, however, often impose constraints that hold throughout the motion: a closed kinematic chain that two grasping arms keep exactly, or joint limits and obstacle clearances that are never crossed. Standard MPPI handles such constraints only through the cost, as soft penalties that hold approximately and fail under a strong task cost. To address this, we propose Projection-Retraction MPPI (PR-MPPI), which enforces the constraints inside the sampled dynamics. At every rollout step, the sampled velocity is projected to satisfy both constraint types: the equality restricts it to a subspace, and each inequality to a half-space within that subspace, so inequality handling never breaks the equality. This projection, however, satisfies the constraints only to first order, and a finite step leaves a small drift off the equality. Therefore, we retract the returned command back onto the constraint, so that the commanded configuration satisfies the equality to numerical tolerance, independently of task weighting. We validate PR-MPPI on 14-DoF dual-arm systems. In simulation, the returned commands satisfy the closed-chain equality to numerical tolerance through a joint-limit stress test and randomized obstacle avoidance, while the measured trajectories retain the joint-limit and obstacle margins. On real hardware, the arms of a Unitree H1-2 humanoid reactively avoid a moving obstacle. Code and experiment videos are available at https://rcilab.khu.ac.kr/prmppi/.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: SiMDex: Mining Similar Egocentric Videos for Cross-Embodiment Dexterous Manipulation
nodes.authors: Nie Lin, Takehiko Ohkawa, Sijin Chen, Ruoshi Wen, Zhuohang Li, Liqun Huang, Zhengming Zhu, Yiming Bao, Yunfei Li, Minjie Cai, Xiao Ma, Wei Xu, Yoichi Sato
nodes.summary: Recent years have witnessed an explosive trend of scaling ego-centric human videos for robot manipulation, yet it remains unclear which data actually benefits dexterous manipulation. We present SiMDex, a similarity-based data mining framework that casts human data selection for VLA post-training in dexterous manipulation as a recommendation problem. For each robot demonstration, SiMDex runs a recall-ranking-re-ranking cascade over ~32M egocentric human samples: two stages, recall and ranking, select a task-relevant subset in a morphology-agnostic action space, and re-ranking verifies it on pixels, with no change to VLA architecture or training. Against a strong baseline trained with an equal amount of randomly sampled human data, SiMDex uses only ~1.49M mined samples (<5% of the pool) yet improves the overall success rate from 47.7% to 61.7%, showing that selective curation outperforms indiscriminate data mixing.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: Flying over The Uncertain Nature (FORTUNE): Intelligent and Humanistic 3D Path Planning for Low-Altitude Collaboration
nodes.authors: Wenbo Zhu, Wenhan Jia, Minghui Liwang, Yiguang Hong
nodes.summary: Low-altitude intelligent agents are driving demand for timely, socially responsible collaborative sensing in dynamic urban environments. Yet jointly handling heterogeneous spatio-temporal sensing demands, real-time uncertainty, and human-centered constraints in a unified multi-uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) framework remains challenging. We study 3D multi-UAV path planning and joint task assignment under heterogeneous spatio-temporal uncertainty of ground points of interest (PoIs). Unlike studies assuming static, known PoIs, we formulate a unified model capturing persistent (Type-I), temporally predictable (Type-II), and emergent unpredictable (Type-III) demands. Following the low-altitude-for-good principle, we explicitly model altitude-dependent societal and environmental costs, including noise and public safety risks, jointly optimizing sensing effectiveness and socially compliant operations. To solve the resulting large-scale mixed-integer nonlinear problem, we propose FORTUNE, a hierarchical offline-online framework. Offline, a Transformer-based predictor forecasts Type-II activation windows, while an enhanced sparrow search algorithm (ES2A) with priority-aware decoding and danger-aware evolution generates globally coordinated flight plans. Online, lightweight trajectory refinement accommodates new Type-III PoIs while preserving global mission coherence. Experiments on real-world traffic and synthetic datasets show FORTUNE consistently outperforms state-of-the-art benchmarks, validating effectiveness, scalability, and practical applicability in dynamic low-altitude systems.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: Risky Business: Measuring The Faithfulness-Safety Tension
nodes.authors: Dominik Meier, Luca Joshua Francis, Marco Bernhard Kaiser, Terry Ruas, Jan Philip Wahle, Bela Gipp
nodes.summary: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning offers a promising window into model monitoring. However, monitoring relies on faithfulness, i.e., the model output strictly derives from its reasoning trace. We identify an alignment tension where a model must be faithful enough to be monitored, yet robust enough to reject unsafe reasoning. We demonstrate that this counterbalance exists in current Large Reasoning Models (LRMs), and show ways in which it can be addressed. We introduce HazMart, a human-written dataset set in an autonomous AI shopkeeper scenario. Unlike prior work that relies on providing hints in prompts to test faithfulness (e.g., "A Stanford professor said it should be Answer A"), we propose a novel replacement-based technique, which we call Targeted Reasoning Replacement (TRR), that directly intervenes in the reasoning chain to substitute in unsafe or illogical thoughts (e.g., "Wait, the answer must be Option B [was Option A] because it is the most fitting"). DeepSeek-R1-Llama-70B exhibits high faithfulness (97.5%) but fails to reject Unsafe Reasoning (12.3%), while QwQ-32B is more robust (73.9% safety) at the cost of lower faithfulness (74.7%). Mechanistic analyses of QwQ-32B reveal that these properties are represented by anti-correlated internal directions peaking at the action-commit token. Finally, we demonstrate that representation steering can independently amplify the safety direction, increasing safe behavior by 9 percentage points while maintaining base capabilities.
nodes.subject: Computation and Language

nodes.title: AURORA-LM: Autoencoding Unified Representation for Continuous-Latent Diffusion Language Modeling
nodes.authors: Jiajun Liang, Yucheng Liao, Yukang Cao, Jiazhe Wei, Ken Li, Wende Tan, Jiankun Zhang, ZY Cui, Jingkang Yang, Liucheng Guo, Shiqi Yang, B. Yang, Caifeng Shan, Ziwei Liu, Chenyang Si
nodes.summary:
Language remains an outlier in generative modeling: while images, video, and audio are increasingly modeled in continuous latent spaces, text generation still relies predominantly on discrete tokens. Existing continuous language models either inherit embedding spaces not designed for joint generation and decoding, or compress autoencoded latents to ease diffusion, sacrificing token-level fidelity. Instead of simplifying the representation to suit the generative model, we preserve a high-capacity, decodable text latent and design the diffusion model to learn its distribution directly.
  We introduce AURORA-LM, a continuous-latent diffusion language model that separates the construction of a decodable text representation from the modeling of its distribution. A Query-based Encoder-Decoder organizes text into a high-capacity, prefix-aligned latent sequence, and a Block-causal Diffusion Transformer learns its distribution through flow matching, generating blocks left to right while denoising positions within each block in parallel. Because such a latent is harder for diffusion to model, AURORA-LM restricts only the noisy-input pathway while retaining the full clean-latent prediction target, accommodating full-width latents without reducing decoder-facing capacity. We further calibrate the noise-level distribution to the latent width, and introduce self-trajectory consistency to bridge independently sampled training noise and iterative denoising at inference.
  AURORA-LM achieves the strongest performance among evaluated continuous and diffusion-based language models on OpenWebText free generation and XSum summarization. Scaling to 1B parameters with about 1500 EFLOPs of total compute yields further gains, surpassing a larger publicly released latent-diffusion language model under a matched evaluation protocol. All experiments are conducted on Ascend NPUs.
nodes.subject: Computation and Language

nodes.title: GeoCore-9B: Towards Geo-Aware Generative Foundation Models in Earth Observation
nodes.authors: Jeonghyeok Do, Munchurl Kim
nodes.summary: Existing generative models for earth observation (EO) predominantly rely on fine-tuning natural image priors, which limits their scalability and introduces perspective biases that conflict with geospatial constraints. To address this, we introduce GeoCore-9B, a 9-billion-parameter generative foundation model, which is the first of its scale to be trained from scratch exclusively on EO data. Unlike previous EO foundation models, GeoCore-9B is built upon a Flow Matching-based Diffusion Transformer (DiT) and natively conditions generation on text descriptions and continuous geospatial metadata, including ground sample distances, latitudes, and longitudes. To overcome the convergence and spatial disorientation challenges of training at this scale, we propose a Geospatial Semantic Alignment loss. This objective distills structural Earth surface priors (e.g., terrain and urban areas) from a frozen specialist teacher network, constraining the diffusion latent trajectory during training without adding inference overhead. Pre-trained on the global-scale Git-10M dataset, GeoCore-9B demonstrates strong downstream versatility. Beyond standard proxy generative tasks, we show that GeoCore-9B can be effectively adapted for practical EO applications, including highly challenging tasks such as cloud removal and SAR-to-optical cross-modal translation. Extensive evaluations confirm that GeoCore-9B establishes new state-of-the-art performance in both visual fidelity and geographic structural accuracy.
nodes.subject: End-to-End AD

nodes.title: Twig: Parallel and Memory-Efficient Tree Speculative Decoding for Hybrid-Attention LLMs
nodes.authors: Li Wang, Yi Su, Xiabao Wu, Chiran You, Yongchao Liu, Zhan Qiu, Juelu Zhang, Jiajun Zheng, Fangxin Liu, Jie Zhang, Chen Tian, Chengying Huan
nodes.summary: Emerging LLMs increasingly interleave full attention with recurrent linear attention to reduce long-context serving costs. Tree speculative decoding could further accelerate these hybrid models, but recurrent linear-attention layers carry parent-dependent states. Existing engines therefore verify proposal trees sequentially and snapshot the full state per node, causing latency and memory to grow with tree and batch sizes. We present Twig, a kernel--runtime co-design for tree speculative decoding of hybrid LLMs. Twig derives a tree-structured factorization of the linear-attention recurrence and realizes it with a resource-efficient GPU kernel that verifies all nodes in parallel, accelerating linear-attention tree verification by 3.4--7.7$\times$. It losslessly represents speculative state updates as token-level factors and reconstructs only the accepted state, reducing transient state memory by 82--99$\times$ and freeing GPU memory for KV caches. We integrate Twig into SGLang, a widely deployed production LLM serving engine, and further optimize its runtime through batch-wide verification budgeting. Across four models, two GPU platforms, and diverse datasets, Twig achieves up to $4.72\times$ the offline decode throughput of autoregressive decoding and up to $2.03\times$ that of the strongest tree-speculative baseline. Under online agent workloads, Twig reduces TTFT and TPOT by up to $67.6\%$ and $49.9\%$, respectively, over the strongest tree-speculative baseline.
nodes.subject: Computation and Language

nodes.title: RADAR Perception for Dynamic Obstacle Avoidance onboard small-scale Quadrotor UAVs
nodes.authors: Dnyandeep Mandaokar, Bernhard Rinner
nodes.summary: Fast dynamic obstacle avoidance (DOA) on uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) demands not only low-latency control and actuation but also reliable, long-range perception to detect obstacles and estimate their motion in time to maneuver. We present, to the best of our knowledge, the first mmWave RADAR-based perception-and-control system for fast onboard DOA. We derive and analyze latency and spatial bounds that relate sensing range, relative speed, and control delay, yielding sufficient conditions for successful avoidance. We further extend prior latency analyses to include the decision latency of the tracker and trigger to evaluate them per trial. Our computationally efficient system combines a lightweight interacting multiple models (IMM) tracker with a control-barrier functions (CBF) controller that directly outputs evasive accelerations. In 300 throw experiments spanning three object sizes and varying visibility (light and dark), it achieves mean position errors of at most 0.15 m, 0.93m, and 0.87m in the x, y, and z directions, with a similar spread in 90 experiments in smoke. An onboard implementation on a Raspberry Pi 4B demonstrates real-time feasibility with an end-to-end processing latency of approximately 14ms per RADAR frame and a system latency of 75ms from first detection to the avoidance command. The UAV successfully avoided obstacles in all 20 tethered indoor flights and all 39 untethered outdoor avoidance maneuvers across three ball sizes, during both hover and forward flights at up to 5m/s with measured closing speeds up to 14.6m/s.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: Characterizing Treatment-Context Medication Evidence Across Clinic Notes and Structured EHR Medication History
nodes.authors: Mingyang Jiang, Congning Ni, Weixin Liu, Zhijun Yin
nodes.summary: Clinic notes may describe medication changes that are not reflected in structured electronic health record (EHR) medication history at the same encounter. Differences in terminology and documentation timing further complicate the interpretation of these discrepancies. We evaluated medication normalization in clinic notes and examined how semantic and temporal matching affected overlap with structured history. A note-grounded reference was constructed from large language model (LLM)-proposed mentions, deterministic canonical projection, and existing targeted correction records; random-audit records were summarized separately. On 5,360 reference mention rows from held-out patients, conditional canonical agreement increased from 81.25% with surface matching to 93.58% after lexical cleanup and curated aliases. Candidate-reference mention alignment was evaluated separately, yielding an F1 score of 0.6547. Across 27,552 reference rows, exact same-visit overlap was 16.71%. Overlap reached 90.22% when ingredient and broad-category matches were permitted at the same visit or within 30 days before or after the note. Incomplete mapping of note-derived labels contributed to residual nonoverlap in ontology-backed comparisons. Exact-label comparison captured only part of the related medication information across sources; broader matches do not establish equivalent medication use or treatment events.
nodes.subject: Computation and Language

nodes.title: Déjà Cue: Localizing States in Object Histories via Vocabulary-Relative Coordinates
nodes.authors: Haofan Cao, Zhichao You, Yunkai Yang, Liang Guo, Jie Wang, Chongshou Li
nodes.summary: Object tracking preserves identity through visual changes, but cannot tell when an object is whole, cut, or peeled. We study state-moment retrieval: locating when a tracked object exhibits each state in a supplied set of descriptions. However, absolute image--text similarity can favor shared object semantics, obscuring the distinctions needed to localize individual states. Our insight is that the alternatives themselves provide a reference for measuring state evidence. We introduce Déjà Cue, a training-free framework that centers description embeddings on a state-balanced vocabulary mean, producing query directions that compare each state against its alternatives. Using frozen vision--language encoders, Déjà Cue calibrates frame scores and retrieves intervals at multiple durations within contiguous visible runs. We construct MS-VOST by annotating 620 object histories with 2,465 states. With the encoder and temporal search fixed, Déjà Cue improves all three localization metrics over absolute scoring across eight encoder configurations, raising Top-1 temporal IoU by 0.42--1.14 percentage points. These gains persist across four text constructions, and candidate-ranking analysis shows that the vocabulary reference brings relevant intervals forward within the same search space. These results establish the supplied state vocabulary as an object-specific reference for localizing semantic states from frozen visual representations.
nodes.subject: Spatial Agents

nodes.title: CoNav-UAV: Cooperative Dual-Altitude Aerial Navigation via Stackelberg Learning
nodes.authors: Junru Song, Wenhao Zhang, Yang Yang, Xuekai Qiu, Feifei Wang, Weien Zhou, Tingsong Jiang, Ying Wen, Yang Li, Wen Yao
nodes.summary: Aerial search missions often require an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) to locate a target from only a brief description of its appearance and surroundings, a task known as target-oriented aerial vision-and-language navigation (VLN). The task demands city-scale exploration and grounding as well as collision-free close-range approach, two interleaved processes that are difficult to reconcile within a single agent. Most existing methods adapt the ground VLN paradigm to a single UAV and rely on external assistance to compensate for its inefficiency. A recent attempt deploys two UAVs at complementary altitudes but still depends on privileged sensing and trains the two agents independently, precluding any mutual adaptation. We propose CoNav-UAV, which models the task as a Stackelberg game between a high-altitude leader and a low-altitude follower to capture their sequential decisions and asymmetric observations and utilities, with both agents using only onboard sensing. We introduce Iterative Stackelberg Learning, which tailors optimization to each agent's role: the leader's high-level vision-language reasoning builds on pretrained capabilities and is refined through memory-based in-context learning, while the follower's precise motion control is fine-tuned through DAgger-style expert distillation. Alternating the two updates lets each agent continually adapt to the other's evolving behavior. CoNav-UAV outperforms single- and dual-agent baselines across three high-fidelity urban scenes from the AerialVLN benchmark. It improves success rate by up to 30.8 points on the learning scene and by up to 9.0 points under cross-scene transfer, where the leader reuses its learned memory and the follower is adapted with 2.6-3.7 times less target-scene data. Extensive ablations confirm the contributions of key components and the benefit of mutual adaptation, with consistent gains across VLM backbones.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: MANGO-Grasp: Mahalanobis Fields over Geometry-Oriented 3D Gaussians for Cross-Embodiment Dexterous Grasping
nodes.authors: Heng Zhang, Kevin Yuchen Ma, Mike Zheng Shou, Weisi Lin, Yan Wu
nodes.summary: Cross-embodiment dexterous grasping aims to synthesize stable grasps across heterogeneous multi-fingered hands with little or no embodiment-specific tuning. Existing interaction-centric methods achieve promising results, but their object representations often underrepresent local surface geometry, hand descriptors do not explicitly capture both morphology and kinematics, and hand-object interaction modeling is typically isotropic. We propose MANGO-Grasp, an anisotropic interaction framework that represents objects as geometry-oriented 3D Gaussian primitives to better preserve local surface geometry, and encodes hands into pretrained descriptors that capture both morphology and kinematics. Hand-object interaction is modeled using anisotropic Mahalanobis fields that reflect the directional nature of contact and guide a shared optimization for grasp realization across embodiments. On the CMAP and MultiGripperGrasp benchmarks, MANGO-Grasp outperforms the strongest seen-hand baseline by up to 8.24 percentage points in simulation. It also transfers zero-shot to the unseen SharpaWave hand, improving over the strongest zero-shot baseline by up to 16.57 percentage points, and achieves 86% success in real-world experiments. The code and additional materials are available at https://connor-zh.github.io/MANGO-Grasp/.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: BODHI: Do LLMs Branch Out and Discover Heterogeneous Inferences?
nodes.authors: Soumadeep Saha, Krish Sharma, Akshay Chaturvedi, Nicholas Asher
nodes.summary: Although reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has improved the reasoning performance of large language models (LLMs), whether it expands reasoning capabilities or primarily improves sampling efficiency remains debated. In this paper, we investigate the nature of test-time exploration in RLVR-trained LLMs by employing controlled maze-solving experiments and BODHI-TREEs, a reusable representation that groups mathematical reasoning segments based on semantic equivalence. These probes help delineate preferences between stylistic variations and semantically distinct continuations. We show that RLVR-trained models exhibit lower candidate preference entropy between semantically distinct continuations than their distilled counterparts, and complementary sampling experiments show lower empirical semantic entropy and fewer observed branches under equal sampling budgets. Thus, policy concentration extends beyond stylistic choices and reduces observed semantic diversity. This reduction coexists with improved constraint adherence and backtracking in mazes, and improved recovery from distracting steps in mathematical reasoning. We conjecture that improved trace validity drives RLVR's sampling-efficiency gains, while policy concentration reduces rollout diversity. Our findings identify a central challenge for RLVR: preserving diverse reasoning trajectories alongside improved trace validity.
nodes.subject: Computation and Language

nodes.title: ReBRAC-v2: The Return of the King
nodes.authors: Denis Tarasov, Robert K. Katzschmann
nodes.summary: Recent offline reinforcement learning methods increasingly rely on expressive generative policies and specialized value guidance. We ask how far systematic modernization of a conventional behavior-regularized actor-critic can go while preserving algorithmic simplicity. ReBRAC-v2 directly trains an exact-likelihood normalizing-flow actor with likelihood, MSE, and MAE behavior regularization, classification-based residual critics, staged optimization, and multi-sample inference. We develop one shared configuration through roughly 600 Bayesian proposals on six OGBench tasks, then adapt only two behavior-regularization coefficients using a 16-point grid for the main comparisons. Across ten common OGBench categories, ReBRAC-v2 averages 74.8 versus 52.3 for the next-best method and ranks first in eight categories. Without structural changes, it also obtains the strongest compared averages on D4RL AntMaze (90.2) and Adroit (33.6). Motivated by these results, we extend evaluation to all 235 state-based single-task problems across the 47 dataset variants in the original OGBench suite. To our knowledge, this is the first complete evaluation in this setting; no compared baseline reports results across the full suite. Per-task scores and configurations establish ReBRAC-v2 as a reference baseline for future work beyond the common task subset. The complete cloning objective retains the highest average after coefficient retuning of its alternatives, while further ablations characterize training, capacity, and inference choices. These results demonstrate the strength of systematic engineering within a minimalist offline RL foundation.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: BiCAA: Bidirectional Credit Assignment for Search-Augmented Agent
nodes.authors: Yibin Huang, Bin Xu, Hailong Cao, Conghui Zhu
nodes.summary: By iteratively retrieving and integrating external evidence, multi-step search enables search-augmented agents to tackle complex question answering. However, vanilla GRPO assigns rewards based solely on final answers, providing limited guidance for intermediate search steps. To provide fine-grained process feedback, we evaluate the value of each search step: it should acquire evidence that advances problem solving while avoiding redundant retrieval. Building on these complementary criteria, we introduce BiCAA, which combines Forward Solvability Gain (FSG) and Subsequent Reasoning Gain (SRG) for bidirectional credit assignment. To reward progress in evidence acquisition, FSG quantifies changes in ground-truth answer likelihood after each interaction. SRG compares the subsequent action's likelihood with and without the current interaction to approximately measure its support for subsequent reasoning, using this support as a proxy signal for non-redundant search to encourage effective and efficient search. BiCAA calibrates local feedback through asymmetric fusion; for policy optimization, it integrates accumulated process rewards with terminal outcome supervision. Across seven open-domain QA benchmarks and two Qwen backbones, experiments show improvements in average F1, particularly on multi-hop tasks.

nodes.title: Dense Language Generation Made Simple: Deterministic, Randomized, and Multi-Order Algorithms
nodes.authors: Ziyi Cai, Shuangping Li, Yiheng Shen, Kangning Wang, Peng Zhang
nodes.summary:
Language generation in the limit is a theoretical framework for studying how a generator can learn to produce new valid strings from a stream of positive examples. In this model, an adversary chooses an unknown language from a countable family and enumerates its elements in an arbitrary order, while the generator must eventually output only elements of the language that have not yet appeared in the enumeration. Reliable generation is thus formalized through two eventual guarantees: validity and novelty relative to the observed data. To further quantify the breadth of the generator's outputs, Kleinberg and Wei (FOCS 2025, STOC 2026) introduced lower density as a measure of output coverage. Given an order representing the importance or relevance of possible outputs, lower density is the asymptotic lower bound, as $n$ grows, on the fraction of the first $n$ elements of the target language that the generator outputs before they appear in the data. Kleinberg and Wei showed that $1/2$ is the optimal lower-density guarantee for deterministic algorithms.
  We develop a simple and unified framework for obtaining optimal lower-density guarantees. We first give a deterministic algorithm that recovers the optimal guarantee of $1/2$ with a significantly simpler analysis than prior work. We then demonstrate the flexibility of our framework through two extensions. First, against an oblivious adversary, randomization raises the optimal guarantee to $1-1/e$. Second, for any finite collection of orders, the optimal deterministic and randomized guarantees can be achieved simultaneously with respect to every order, so accommodating multiple notions of importance or relevance entails no loss in the optimal guarantee.

nodes.title: Gaokerena: A Small Persian Medical Language Model Family
nodes.authors: Mehrdad Ghassabi, Hamidreza Baradaran Kashani, Pedram Rostami, Sadra Hakim, Zahra Kazemi, Amirhossein Poursina, Milad Tavakoli, Audrina Ebrahimi
nodes.summary: Persian medical natural language processing remains limited by the scarcity of domain-specific resources and insufficient public characterization of their coverage and quality. We present Gaokerena, an openly released suite of Persian medical resources comprising an 85.5-million-word corpus of 101,954 web articles; MF3QA, a 24,000-pair patient-doctor question-answering dataset; 1,878 Iranian medical examination questions (KOPP); 1,089 manually translated medical MMLU questions (FA_MED_MMLU); and approximately 18,000 machine-translated MedMCQA training items filtered by two language-model evaluators. We characterize the resources' composition, orthographic variation, redundancy, topical coverage, privacy indicators, answer-key balance, extraction artefacts, and translation limitations. As application case studies, we adapt Aya-Expanse-8B into Gaokerena-V, trained on the corpus and MF3QA, and Gaokerena-R, developed through preference-based reasoning distillation. On translated medical MMLU, Gaokerena-V achieves 49.31% accuracy under direct prompting, compared with 46.65% for Aya-Expanse-8B; the paired exact McNemar test is statistically inconclusive (p = 0.0502). Gaokerena-R reaches 52.80% using five-sample self-consistency and a verifier, but this higher-compute setting is not directly comparable. Under matched five-sample chain-of-thought self-consistency without a verifier, Gaokerena-R scores 48.58%, versus 46.92% for Aya-Expanse-8B, a non-significant difference (p = 0.190). English evaluation also reveals a substantial performance gap relative to Persian. To our knowledge, Gaokerena provides the first openly released and systematically characterized suite of Persian medical resources alongside generative models built on them. These protocol-specific results do not establish an isolated training advantage or clinical readiness.

nodes.title: UDT: Reconciling U-Nets and Diffusion Transformers with Data-Adaptive Token Reduction
nodes.authors: Junno Yun, Yaşar Utku Alçalar, Mehmet Akçakaya
nodes.summary: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) have emerged as a core architecture in generative modeling due to their scalability and adaptability to multimodal tasks. DiTs comprise isotropic transformer blocks, and learn representations progressively across depth, where the denoising objective drives later layers to focus on fine-detail reconstruction. This results in degraded representation quality and an imbalanced encoder-decoder behavior. Prior approaches such as representation alignment (REPA) mitigate this by encouraging stronger early representations via training regularization. Alternatively, U-Net-style DiT architectures introduce explicit multi-scale encoder-decoder structures for improved convergence. But they build on standard U-Net wisdom via learnable operators for spatial downsampling, which are not well-suited to transformer architectures, introducing inefficiencies and compatibility issues with components such as cross-attention and representation regularization. In this work, we propose UDT, a U-Net diffusion transformer that combines the representation power of DiTs with the encoding-decoding benefits of U-Nets, through data-adaptive token merging for downsampling and upsampling, while preserving the DiT token dimension. Our baseline UDT architecture outperforms existing U-Net DiTs and achieves performance comparable to REPA across all model sizes. Furthermore, using architectural optimization and REPA, UDT outperforms SiT's 7.9 FID at 1400 epochs (w/o CFG) within 40 epochs (~ 40x faster convergence) for XL model size on 256x256 ImageNet. Finally, it achieves strong image generation performance with CFG, reaching FID of 1.38 (320 epochs) with SD-VAE and 1.35 (500 epochs) with VA-VAE, providing a new backbone for DiTs with strong empirical benefits. Code is available at https://github.com/JN-Yun/UDT
nodes.subject: 3D Vision

nodes.title: You Don't Need To Stay in The Loop: An Agentic Robotics Loop for Robot-Policy Improvement
nodes.authors: Hang Yu
nodes.summary: Coding agents close the software loop for training a robot policy without having a human in the loop: a main agent manages the training, subagents analyze and execute, treat robot policies and hardware as tools and do the work. We port this architecture to robot-policy improvement, where one difference dominates the design: robotic tools such as trained policies, training pipelines, and data collection fail routinely, so a tool's quality must be measured, recorded at every call, and expired when the artifact behind it changes. AgenticRobotics is a backend-independent control plane in which an LLM controller drives disposable workers through durable train--evaluate--improve transactions: an immutable objective, controller-owned measurement, commit-keyed crash recovery, an evidence-graded skill library, and a tool registry with a standardized, recorded call surface. The title is an operational claim, not a selection claim: the operator can leave because promotion is evidence-gated, state is recoverable, and capability quality is derived from records, not because the loop picks better checkpoints than a human. On the one lineage we measured, it does not. The gates provide measured false-promotion control (0.001 false promotions per run with the hardened margin, against 0.005--0.021 with the shipped rule), anytime-valid decisions under optional stopping, zero lost or duplicate effects under kill injection, and a signed verifier that caught six of six artifact-tampering classes.

nodes.title: Tevatron Meets Megatron: Expert-Parallel LLM Reranker Training on an Academic Budget
nodes.authors: Zhichao Xu, Xueguang Ma, Shengyao Zhuang, Luyu Gao, Wenqian Ye, Yu Wang, Jamie Callan, Jimmy Lin
nodes.summary: Training large dense and mixture-of-experts (MoE) rerankers is constrained by GPU memory and distributed-execution efficiency, which has kept academic reranker research largely on dense models. Tevatron trains rerankers through the Hugging Face Trainer with DeepSpeed and PyTorch FSDP1, a stack that stalls on three fronts: DeepSpeed ZeRO-2 has a known gradient-gathering failure on this path, FSDP1 full sharding is memory-safe but throughput-bound, and neither offers the expert parallelism (EP) that MoE training needs. We present Tevatron 3.0, which integrates Megatron-Core as a reranker training backend while preserving Tevatron's data processing, evaluation pipeline, and Hugging Face checkpoint format. For full-parameter dense 8B training, Megatron matches FSDP1 on BEIR-15 NDCG@10 with approximately 4% lower epoch time and twice the peak GPU memory under matched data-parallel and recomputation settings, and approximately 22% lower epoch time in its recommended configuration; it supports both LoRA and full-parameter fine-tuning. Expert parallelism makes it possible to train a 30B-parameter MoE reranker (Qwen3-30B-A3B) on two nodes. A controlled study of architecture, LoRA, and distillation on BEIR-15, with three first-stage retrievers and Hugging Face and vLLM serving, shows that the MoE reranker matches dense-8B quality at less than half the activated parameters and at higher inference throughput. We open-source the framework and trained checkpoints.

nodes.authors: Mehrdad Ghassabi, Hamidreza Baradaran Kashani, Pedram Rostami, Sadra Hakim, Zahra Kazemi, Amirhossein Poursina, Milad Tavakoli, Audrina Ebrahimi

nodes.title: Observatorio Lazaro: A self-populating database of anglicism usage in the Spanish press
nodes.authors: Elena Alvarez-Mellado
nodes.summary: This paper describes Observatorio Lázaro, a language resource that monitors unassimilated lexical borrowings (predominantly English lexical borrowings or anglicisms) in the Spanish digital press. Since April 2020 the system has automatically processed the daily output of a collection of news outlets, detected borrowings with a neural sequence-labeling model, and made the results available through a public web interface and API. The result is a continuously updated diachronic database which, at the time of writing, records more than two million borrowings across 1.88 million articles and 993 million running tokens of text (2020-2026). The paper documents the resource: we describe the end-to-end pipeline (acquisition, detection, post-processing, storage and access), the data model and the terms of availability; we evaluate the resource through the detector's held-out performance (span-level F1=0.86 for the borrowing class), inter-annotator agreement on the training corpus (Cohen's kappa=0.91) and a manual precision audit of 1,000 spans from the deployed data; and we situate it with respect to Spanish borrowing lexicography, annotated borrowing corpora and neology-monitoring observatories. The data shows that unassimilated anglicisms are used in the Spanish press at a frequency of approximately two anglicisms per thousand tokens, and that this rate remains stable. Our statistical analysis over six years reveals that the anglicism vocabulary in Spanish behaves as an open and growing class, with 58.7% of its types attested only once (53.6% after correcting for detection precision), and that its density is highest in the fashion, technology and lifestyle sections and lowest in political and institutional news. The resource is intended to complement static borrowing dictionaries and one-off annotated corpora by providing a continuously updated record of borrowing in the Spanish press.
