We present DiTGaze, a calibration-efficient augmentation system that follows a two-stream 3D Gaussian Splatting backbone and reformulates its convolutional rendering stage as a geometry-conditioned latent Diffusion Transformer (DiT). A learnable projection and frozen VAE bridge rasterized Gaussian features to latent tokens, while timestep and identity/expression conditioning are integrated through Adaptive Layer Normalization. Intermediate yaw-pitch sampling densifies gaze supervision, and an orthogonality constraint reduces interference between gaze, pose, and expression. On ETH-XGaze, DiTGaze reduces generator-level gaze error by 4.1 percent relative to GazeGaussian. In our runs of the expanded downstream protocol, it ranks first at every calibration budget from one to nine real images; the repeated primary comparison at N = 9 reduces subject-level estimator error by 0.73 degrees and improves 14 of 15 identities (p < 0.001). These results connect the proposed generator changes to statistically supported few-shot personalization gains.
nodes.subject: 3D Vision

nodes.title: A Systematic Analysis of Out-of-Distribution Detection Under Representation and Training Paradigm Shifts
nodes.authors: Claudio César Claros Olivares, Austin J. Brockmeier
nodes.summary: We present a systematic benchmark of out-of-distribution (OOD) detection confidence scoring functions (CSFs) through a representation-centric lens. Our study spans CNN and ViT backbones, multiple training paradigms, four image-classification source datasets (CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SuperCIFAR-100, and TinyImageNet), and OOD datasets grouped into near, mid, and far regimes based on CLIP-derived semantic distances. To compare CSFs across these settings, we employ a rank-based pipeline of Friedman and Conover tests that identifies top cliques of statistically indistinguishable winners under threshold-free ranking metrics (AURC and AUGRC). The main empirical finding is that the family of CSFs that are competitive detectors correlates with characteristics of the learned representation. For both CNNs and ViTs, simple probabilistic scores dominate misclassification detection. On CNNs, margin-based scores are strongest in near-OOD regimes, while geometry-aware scores such as NNGuide, fDBD, and CTM become more competitive as shift severity increases. On fine-tuned ViTs, the top cliques are led mainly by reconstruction- and residual-based scores. To interpret these ranking shifts, we analyze the last-layer representation using Neural Collapse (NC) metrics. The resulting picture is consistent across architectures: prototype- and boundary-aware scores become stronger when the representation is more collapsed and better aligned with classifier weights, whereas weaker-collapse regimes favor gradient- and manifold-based scores. Building on these insights, we propose two contributions: a simple PCA-based projection-filtering procedure that improves detector performance, and an approach that uses only the NC measurements of a trained classifier to predict its competitive out-of-distribution detector shortlist, without OOD data for that classifier and without knowledge of the shift.
nodes.subject: NeRF

nodes.title: Sparse corruption in low-rank matrix inference: the PCA benchmark
nodes.authors: Urte Adomaityte, Gabriele Sicuro, Pierpaolo Vivo
nodes.summary: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is a standard tool for extracting a low-rank signal from noisy observations. It is known that when applying PCA to a rank-one signal corrupted by a dense, homogeneous noise, in the large matrix size limit, the BBP transition occurs, where the emergence of an outlying eigenvalue and the alignment of the corresponding eigenvector occur at the same critical signal strength. Here we study the case of sparse noise corruption. The noise matrix is modelled as the adjacency matrix of a weighted undirected graph with finite average connectivity. Using the replica method, we analytically compute the typical top eigenvalue, the top eigenvector component density, and the overlap with the signal, through recursive distributional equations solved by population dynamics. We identify two signal-strength transitions as functions of graph connectivity: $θ_{\rm crit}$, marking signal recovery by the top eigenvector and generalising the BBP transition, and $θ_{\rm b}$, where the signal-related eigenvalue detaches from the bulk. For noise with nonzero mean, these transitions need not coincide because of a structural sparse-graph outlier, leading to a discontinuous transition in the overlap with the top eigenvector. For a Random Regular degree distribution, we obtain exact closed-form expressions for both thresholds, the signal eigenvalue and the squared overlap, and show that the same formulas also predict the overlap of the signal with the second eigenvector in the intermediate regime $θ_{\rm b}<θ\leq θ_{\rm crit}$. For a Poissonian degree distribution, an approximate closure of the recursions yields fast and accurate predictions in the recovery phase that agree with exact results from population dynamics. We also recover dense-noise results in the large-connectivity limit, and validate the theory by numerical diagonalisation of large matrices.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: StochEP: Stochastic Equilibrium Propagation for Spiking Convergent Recurrent Neural Networks
nodes.authors: Jiaqi Lin, Yi Jiang, Abhronil Sengupta
nodes.summary: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) promise energy-efficient, sparse, biologically inspired computation. Training them with Backpropagation Through Time (BPTT) and surrogate gradients achieves strong performance but remains biologically implausible. Equilibrium Propagation (EP) provides a more local and biologically grounded alternative. However, existing EP frameworks for SNNs largely rely on deterministic neurons, which require complex mechanisms to handle spiking discontinuities and do not scale beyond simple benchmarks such as MNIST and Fashion-MNIST. Inspired by the stochastic nature of biological spiking mechanism and recent hardware trends, we propose a stochastic EP framework that integrates probabilistic spiking neurons into the EP paradigm. This formulation smoothens the optimization landscape, stabilizes training, and enables efficient and scalable learning in SNNs. We provide theoretical guarantees showing that the proposed stochastic EP dynamics approximate deterministic EP under mean-field theory, thereby inheriting its underlying theoretical guarantees. The proposed framework narrows the performance gap with both BPTT-trained SNNs and EP-trained non-spiking convergent recurrent neural networks (CRNNs) on CIFAR-10, DVS Gesture, and IMDB datasets, while preserving temporal and spatial locality. Our results highlight stochastic EP as a promising approach for neuromorphic and on-chip learning.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: Lumos3D: A Single-Forward Framework for Low-Light 3D Scene Restoration
nodes.authors: Hanzhou Liu, Peng Jiang, Jia Huang, Mi Lu
nodes.summary: Restoring 3D scenes with low-light conditions is challenging, and most existing methods depend on precomputed camera poses and scene-specific optimization, which greatly restricts their application to real-world scenarios. To overcome these limitations, we propose Lumos3D, a pose-free single-forward framework for 3D low-light scene restoration. First, we develop a cross-illumination distillation scheme, where a frozen teacher network takes normal-light ground truth images as input to distill accurate geometric information to the student model. Second, we define a Lumos loss to improve the restoration quality of the reconstructed 3D Gaussian space. Trained on a single dataset, Lumos3D performs inference in a purely feed-forward manner, directly restoring illumination and structure from unposed, low-light multi-view images without any per-scene training or optimization. Experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that Lumos3D achieves competitive restoration results compared to scene-specific methods. Our codes are available at https://github.com/HanzhouLiu/Lumos3D.
nodes.subject: 3D Vision

nodes.title: Multi-objective Hyperparameter Optimization with Expert Priors
nodes.authors: Soham Basu, Nastaran Alipour, Frank Hutter, Danny Stoll
nodes.summary: While Deep Learning (DL) experts often have prior knowledge about which hyperparameter settings yield strong performance, only few Hyperparameter Optimization (HPO) algorithms can leverage such prior knowledge and none incorporate priors over multiple objectives. As DL practitioners often need to optimize not just one but many objectives, this is a blind spot in the algorithmic landscape of HPO. To address this shortcoming, we propose the novel problem setting of multi-objective HPO with expert priors and introduce PriMO, the first HPO algorithm that can integrate user beliefs over multiple objectives. We show PriMO achieves state-of-the-art performance across 8 DL benchmarks in the multi-objective and single-objective setting. Further, we demonstrate that PriMO remains state-of-the-art at large scales by optimizing a vision-language model over three objectives.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: NeuroBridge: Bio-Inspired Self-Supervised EEG-to-Image Decoding via Cognitive Priors and Bidirectional Semantic Alignment
nodes.authors: Wenjiang Zhang, Sifeng Wang, Yuwei Su, Xinyu Li, Chen Zhang, Suyu Zhong
nodes.summary: Visual neural decoding seeks to reconstruct or infer perceived visual stimuli from brain activity patterns, providing critical insights into human cognition and enabling transformative applications in brain-computer interfaces and artificial intelligence. Current approaches, however, remain constrained by the scarcity of high-quality stimulus-brain response pairs and the inherent semantic mismatch between neural representations and visual content. Inspired by perceptual variability and co-adaptive strategy of the biological systems, we propose a novel self-supervised architecture, named NeuroBridge, which integrates Cognitive Prior Augmentation (CPA) with Shared Semantic Projector (SSP) to promote effective cross-modality alignment. Specifically, CPA simulates perceptual variability by applying asymmetric, modality-specific transformations to both EEG signals and images, enhancing semantic diversity. Unlike previous approaches, SSP establishes a bidirectional alignment process through a co-adaptive strategy, which mutually aligns features from two modalities into a shared semantic space for effective cross-modal learning. NeuroBridge surpasses previous state-of-the-art methods under both intra-subject and inter-subject settings. In the intra-subject scenario, it achieves the improvements of 12.3% in top-1 accuracy and 10.2% in top-5 accuracy, reaching 63.2% and 89.9% respectively on a 200-way zero-shot retrieval task. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness, robustness, and scalability of the proposed framework for neural visual decoding.
nodes.subject: 3D Vision

nodes.title: KGBridge: Knowledge-Guided Prompt Learning for Non-overlapping Cross-Domain Recommendation
nodes.authors: Yuhan Wang, Qing Xie, Zhifeng Bao, Mengzi Tang, Lin Li, Yongjian Liu
nodes.summary:
Knowledge Graphs (KGs) provide structured relational information, offering a unified semantic foundation for cross-domain recommendation (CDR). Integrating symbolic knowledge with interactions enriches representations, supports reasoning, and enhances interpretability. However, existing methods face three major challenges: (C1) sensitivity to KG sparsity and popularity bias, (C2) reliance on overlapping users for domain alignment, and (C3) insufficient disentanglement between transferable and domain-specific knowledge, which limits stable knowledge transfer.
  To address these challenges, this paper proposes KGBridge, a knowledge-guided prompt learning framework for non-overlapping cross-domain sequential recommendation. KGBridge comprises: (i) a KG-enhanced prompt encoder that models relation-level semantics as soft prompts, providing structured priors for sequential preference modeling (for C1), and (ii) a two-stage training paradigm combining cross-domain pretraining with privacy-preserving fine-tuning to enable knowledge transfer without shared users (for C2). Furthermore, via correspondence-driven disentanglement, KGBridge explicitly separates domain-shared and domain-specific semantics, preserving their complementarity and stabilizing target-domain adaptation (for C3). Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that KGBridge consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines and exhibits robustness under varying KG sparsity, confirming its effectiveness in alleviating structural imbalance and semantic entanglement. To facilitate reproducibility, the source code and datasets are publicly available at https://github.com/WangYuhan-0520/KGBridge.
nodes.subject: Information Retrieval

nodes.title: Speech-DRAME: A Framework for Human-Aligned Benchmarks in Speech Role-Play
nodes.authors: Jiatong Shi, Jionghao Han, Yichen Lu, Santiago Pascual, Pengfei Wu, Chenye Cui, Shinji Watanabe, Chao Weng, Cong Zhou
nodes.summary: Evaluating spoken role-play requires judging not only linguistic content but also prosody, emotional expression, character embodiment, and contextual fit. Existing automatic evaluation methods often collapse these aspects into coarse scores and are evaluated primarily on synthesized speech. We introduce Speech-DRAME, a framework comprising Speech-DRAME-EvalBench, a bilingual, human-annotated benchmark with contrastive role-, context-, and delivery-mismatch conditions, and DRAME-Eval, a fine-tuned audio-language evaluator. The benchmark supports two complementary protocols: top-down archetype evaluation and bottom-up realism evaluation, with predominantly synthesized benchmark-distribution data and a held-out stress test consisting entirely of authentic human acting. On the benchmark-distribution sets, DRAME-Eval achieves pooled Pearson correlations of 0.629 for archetype evaluation and 0.602 for realism evaluation, significantly outperforming the evaluated zero- and few-shot audio-language judges; modality controls show that its judgments depend on both speech and textual context. This alignment does not transfer to the authentic-speech test set, where DRAME-Eval obtains an average correlation of -0.142 and a within-speaker correlation of +0.029, compared with matched human single-rater agreement of +0.34. These results identify a substantial synthetic-to-authentic transfer gap and establish Speech-DRAME as a resource for studying and improving evaluation of acting differences among real human performances.
nodes.subject: Embodied Intelligence

nodes.title: Vote-in-Context: Turning VLMs into Zero-Shot Rank Fusers
nodes.authors: Mohamed Eltahir, Ali Habibullah, Lama Ayash, Tanveer Hussain, Naeemullah Khan
nodes.summary: In the retrieval domain, candidates' fusion from heterogeneous retrievers is a long-standing challenge, particularly for complex, multi-modal data such as videos. While typical fusion techniques are training-free, they rely solely on rank or score signals, disregarding candidates' representations. This work introduces Vote-in-Context (ViC), a generalized, training-free framework that re-thinks list-wise reranking and fusion as a zero-shot reasoning task for a Vision-Language Model (VLM). The core insight is to serialize both content evidence and retriever metadata directly within the VLM's prompt, allowing the model to adaptively weigh retriever consensus against visual-linguistic content. We demonstrate the generality of this framework by applying it to the challenging domain of cross-modal video retrieval. To this end, we introduce the S-Grid, a compact serialization map that represents each video as an image grid, optionally paired with subtitles to enable list-wise reasoning over video candidates. ViC is evaluated both as a single-list reranker, where it dramatically improves the precision of individual retrievers, and as an ensemble fuser, where it consistently outperforms strong baselines like CombSUM. Across video retrieval benchmarks including ActivityNet and VATEX, the framework establishes new state-of-the-art zero-shot retrieval performance, demonstrating its effectiveness in handling complex visual and temporal signals alongside text. In zero-shot settings, ViC achieves Recall@1 scores of 87.1% (t2v) / 89.0% (v2t) on MSR-VTT and 99.6% (v2t) on VATEX, representing massive gains of up to +40 Recall@1 over previous state-of-the-art baselines. We present ViC as a simple, reproducible, and highly effective recipe for turning modern VLMs into powerful zero-shot rerankers and fusers. Code and resources are publicly available at: https://github.com/mohammad2012191/ViC
nodes.subject: Information Retrieval

nodes.title: SEPS: Semantic-enhanced Patch Slimming Framework for fine-grained cross-modal alignment
nodes.authors: Xinyu Mao, Junsi Li, Haoji Zhang, Yu Liang, Ming Sun
nodes.summary: Fine-grained cross-modal alignment aims to establish precise local correspondences between vision and language, forming a cornerstone for visual question answering and related multimodal applications. Current approaches face challenges in addressing patch redundancy and ambiguity, which arise from the inherent information density disparities across modalities. Recently, Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have emerged as promising solutions to bridge this gap through their robust semantic generation capabilities. However, the dense textual outputs from MLLMs may introduce conflicts with the original sparse captions. Furthermore, accurately quantifying semantic relevance between rich visual patches and concise textual descriptions remains a core challenge. To overcome these limitations, we introduce the Semantic-Enhanced Patch Slimming (SEPS) framework, which systematically addresses patch redundancy and ambiguity. Our approach employs a two-stage mechanism to integrate unified semantics from both dense and sparse texts, enabling the identification of salient visual patches. Additionally, it leverages relevance-aware selection with mean value computation to highlight crucial patch-word correspondences, thereby improving cross-modal similarity assessment. Comprehensive experiments on Flickr30K and MS-COCO datasets validate that SEPS achieves superior performance, surpassing existing approaches by 23\%-86\% in rSum across diverse model architectures, with notable enhancements in text-to-image retrieval scenarios. Our implementation is available at https://github.com/Sweet4tars/seps.git.
nodes.subject: Multimedia

nodes.title: MAESTRO: Orchestrating Robotics Modules with Coding Agents for Zero-Shot Generalist Robots
nodes.authors: Junyao Shi, Rujia Yang, Kaitian Chao, Selina Bingqing Wan, Yifei Shao, Jiahui Lei, Jianing Qian, Long Le, Pratik Chaudhari, Kostas Daniilidis, Chuan Wen, Dinesh Jayaraman
nodes.summary: Today's dominant route to generalist robots scales robotics data to train end-to-end policies. We instead use a vision-language model (VLM) as a coding agent that writes robot programs using a curated library of perception, planning, and control tools. MAESTRO's orchestration harness packages multi-step perception and action procedures into callable tools and guides their use through a plan-act-replan loop, using visual and execution feedback to verify outcomes and recover from failures. With this tool library and harness, MAESTRO matches or surpasses state-of-the-art vision-language-action (VLA) models zero-shot in our tabletop comparison and performs diverse mobile manipulation tasks, without collecting new teleoperation data or invoking a VLA tool. Ablations show that expanding the tool library improves average task progress with the full harness, while adding tools without it does not reliably improve progress. Case studies illustrate MAESTRO's potential for autonomous code improvement across trials, faster execution with VLA tools, and automatic robot data generation. We show that expanding robotics tool libraries together with their orchestration harnesses offers a complementary route to general-purpose robots alongside scaling end-to-end robot training data. Project site: https://maestro-robot.github.io. Code: https://github.com/penn-pal-lab/maestro.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: Formalizing Heterogeneous Interaction Modeling for Multi-Agent Debate in Visual Geo-Localization
nodes.authors: Zijie Zhou, Dandan Zhu, Heng Zhang, Yanming Yang, Xu Liu, Huishen Jiao
nodes.summary: Visual geo-localization requires complex reasoning to infer image locations without GPS metadata. Traditional retrieval methods are limited by database quality while Large Vision Language Models often struggle with diverse scenes. Although existing multi-agent systems improve collaboration, they treat interactions uniformly and lack effective conflict resolution. We propose GraphGeo, a multi-agent debate framework based on heterogeneous graph neural networks for visual geo-localization. The framework models diverse debate relationships through typed edges and separates supportive collaboration, competitive argumentation and knowledge transfer. We introduce a dual-level debate mechanism combining node-level refinement and edge-level argumentation modeling. A cross-level topology refinement strategy enables co-evolution between graph structure and agent representations. Experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate GraphGeo outperforms single model and multi-agent baselines. The framework converts cognitive conflicts between agents into higher geo-localization accuracy through structured debate.
nodes.subject: NeRF

nodes.title: Learning Soft Robotic Dynamics with Active Exploration
nodes.authors: Hehui Zheng, Bhavya Sukhija, Chenhao Li, Klemens Iten, Andreas Krause, Robert K. Katzschmann
nodes.summary: Soft robots offer adaptability and safety in unstructured environments, yet their compliant, high-dimensional, and nonlinear dynamics make modeling for control difficult. Existing data-driven approaches often fail to generalize, constrained by narrowly focused task demonstrations or inefficient random exploration. We introduce an uncertainty-aware active exploration framework that autonomously learns task-agnostic and generalizable dynamics models of soft robotic systems. We evaluate this framework on three simulated platforms---a continuum arm, an articulated fish in fluid, and a musculoskeletal leg---and on a real-world pneumatically actuated continuum arm. Compared with random exploration and task-specific baseline, our method achieves higher modeling accuracy by actively collecting informative data. This improved model quality yields higher returns in zero-shot control on unseen tasks and robust performance under sensing noise, actuation delays, and material nonlinearities. These results demonstrate that uncertainty-driven active exploration enables data-efficient dynamics learning across soft robotic morphologies, supporting autonomous and adaptable control for compliant robots.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: Diffusion LLMs are Natural Adversaries for any LLM
nodes.authors: David Lüdke, Tom Wollschläger, Paul Ungermann, Stephan Günnemann, Leo Schwinn
nodes.summary: We introduce a novel framework that transforms the resource-intensive (adversarial) prompt optimization problem into an \emph{efficient, amortized inference task}. Our core insight is that pretrained, non-autoregressive generative LLMs, such as Diffusion LLMs, which model the joint distribution over prompt-response pairs, can serve as powerful surrogates for prompt search. This approach enables direct conditional generation of prompts, effectively replacing costly discrete optimization with a small number of parallelizable samples. We provide a probabilistic analysis demonstrating that under mild fidelity assumptions, only a few conditional samples are required to recover high-reward (harmful) prompts. Empirically, our method substantially outperforms prior attacks in both success rate and compute cost, producing low-perplexity, diverse jailbreaks that transfer to a wide range of black-box target models, including robustly trained and proprietary LLMs. Beyond adversarial prompting, our framework opens new directions for red teaming, automated prompt optimization, and leveraging emerging Flow- and Diffusion-based LLMs.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: Estimation of aboveground biomass in a tropical dry forest: An intercomparison of airborne, unmanned, and space laser scanning
nodes.authors: Nelson Mattié, Arturo Sanchez-Azofeifa, Pablo Crespo-Peremarch, Juan-Ygnacio López-Hernández
nodes.summary: Accurate aboveground biomass (AGB) estimates are needed to report forest carbon under the Paris Agreement, yet tropical dry forests (TDFs) remain among the least studied tropical ecosystems. We present a plot-level intercomparison of airborne (ALS), unmanned (ULS) and simulated spaceborne full-waveform (SLS, GEDI simulator) laser scanning for AGB estimation in ten permanent plots of Santa Rosa National Park, Costa Rica, covering early to late succession. Reference AGB (22-220 Mg/ha) was computed from the 2021 census with a documented procedure that screens diameter time series and propagates measurement, wood-density and allometric errors (plot uncertainty 3.5-14.5%). We compared ordinary least squares (OLS), a log-log model of mean canopy height fixed a priori and a single-metric model selected from the data, with support vector machine regression (SVM). Predictor selection, scaling and hyper-parameter tuning were nested within leave-one-plot-out validation. ALS gave the lowest errors: the a priori OLS model reached an RMSE of 32.3 Mg/ha (29%, R2_LOO = 0.77) and SVM 35.8 Mg/ha (32%). SVM did not improve on OLS for any platform and was significantly worse with ULS (p = 0.01). The best ULS and SLS models reached 33% and 37%; differences between platforms were not significant with ten plots. Selecting predictors on all plots before cross-validation lowered the apparent SVM error by up to 23 percentage points, and footprint coordinates, ALS point density and terrain elevation from the GEDI simulator produced spurious skill; these effects explain the higher accuracies reported in an earlier version of this work. Model errors remained at least 2.5 times larger than the field-AGB uncertainty. With small plot networks, a height-based OLS model with ALS is the most robust choice, and more and larger plots are needed before nonlinear models can be shown to add value in TDFs.
nodes.subject: Generative POI Search and Recommendation

nodes.title: Supervised Fine-tuning for Geometry-aware Instruction-following
nodes.authors: Allen Schmaltz
nodes.summary: We examine a contrastive input encoding scheme for supervised fine-tuning of language models (LMs) that masks the content of incorrect generations up to a classification control token. This small-scale study, using a variation of the classic word ordering diagnostic task, suggests this straightforward approach generally preserves the generation accuracy of supervised fine-tuning that uses only positive examples, while increasing the admission rate of generations in the calibrated high-probability region of a Similarity-Distance-Magnitude (SDM) estimator for binary classification of instruction-following. At the same time, we corroborate existing evidence that constructing a calibrated SDM estimator, which models the geometry of the feature-representation space, is not strictly dependent on specialized fine-tuning of the underlying LM's parameters.
nodes.subject: Computation and Language

nodes.title: A Framework for Bounding Deterministic Risk with PAC-Bayes: Applications to Majority Votes
nodes.authors: Benjamin Leblanc, Pascal Germain
nodes.summary: PAC-Bayes is a popular and efficient framework for obtaining generalization guarantees in situations involving uncountable hypothesis spaces. Unfortunately, in its classical formulation, it only provides guarantees on the expected risk of a randomly sampled hypothesis. This requires stochastic predictions at test time, making PAC-Bayes unusable in many practical situations where a single deterministic hypothesis must be deployed. We propose a unified framework for extracting guarantees for a single hypothesis from PAC-Bayesian guarantees. We present a general derandomization framework, and derive from it a numerical bound for majority votes and for three different probability distributions over the posterior space. We study the empirical behaviour of our approach, showing that it consistently outperforms popular baselines in terms of generalization bounds for single classifiers (by up to a factor of 2), but sometimes requires a sacrifice in accuracy.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: Generalizing Test-time Compute-optimal Scaling as an Optimizable Graph
nodes.authors: Fali Wang, Jihai Chen, Shuhua Yang, Runxue Bao, Tianxiang Zhao, Zhiwei Zhang, Xianfeng Tang, Hui Liu, Qi He, Suhang Wang
nodes.summary: Test-Time Scaling (TTS) improves large language models (LLMs) by allocating additional computation during inference, typically through parallel, sequential, or hybrid scaling. However, prior studies often assume fixed collaboration architectures (e.g., topologies) and single-model usage, overlooking that optimal architectures and model combinations can vary across tasks. Therefore, we study the novel problem of searching for compute-optimal model combinations and architectures in TTS under a fixed budget. We formalize it as a multi-LLM collaboration graph, where nodes encode roles and LLM model assignments, and edges capture information flow. This problem is challenging because (i) the combinatorial search space is prohibitively large, and (ii) task-specific requirements demand tailored designs. To address these, we reformulate the problem as probabilistic graph optimization and, through pilot experiments, derive three empirical insights into TTS collaboration graphs. Guided by these insights, we propose Agent-REINFORCE, an LLM-agent-augmented framework that mirrors the REINFORCE pipeline by mapping sampling-gradient-update to sampling-feedback-update, where feedback serves as a textual gradient to update the probabilistic graph and efficiently search for optimal multi-LLM collaboration graphs. Experiments show that Agent-REINFORCE outperforms both traditional and LLM-based baselines in sample efficiency and search performance, and effectively identifies optimal graphs under joint objectives of accuracy and inference latency.
nodes.subject: Computation and Language

nodes.title: DEBATE: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Evaluating Opinion Dynamics in Role-Playing LLM Agents
nodes.authors: Yun-Shiuan Chuang, Ruixuan Tu, Chengtao Dai, You Li, Smit Vasani, Binwei Yao, Michael Henry Tessler, Sijia Yang, Dhavan Shah, Robert Hawkins, Junjie Hu, Timothy T. Rogers
nodes.summary: Modeling opinion change through social interactions is important for understanding polarization, misinformation, and societal conflict. Recent work simulates opinion dynamics with role-playing LLM agents (RPLAs), but multi-agent simulations often display unnatural group behavior (e.g., premature convergence) and lack empirical benchmarks for assessing alignment with real human group interactions. We introduce DEBATE, a benchmark for evaluating the authenticity of opinion dynamics in multi-agent RPLA simulations. Its three-round design makes each participant's public interaction history complete and traceable. DEBATE contains multi-round public messages and private Likert-scale beliefs from U.S.-based participants across 107 topics. The dataset covers 2,788 participants in 697 groups, enabling evaluation at the utterance and group levels. We instantiate "digital twin" RPLAs with seven LLMs and evaluate across two settings: Next Message Prediction and Full Dynamics Simulation, using stance-based opinion-dynamics metrics. In zero-shot settings, RPLA groups exhibit strong opinion convergence relative to human groups. Across group-generalization tests with unseen participant groups and topic-generalization tests with unseen discussion topics, supervised fine-tuning (SFT) of Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen3.5-4B, and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 improves stance-based alignment and reduces excessive convergence, bringing RPLA group convergence closer to that observed in the corresponding human groups, though discrepancies in opinion change and belief updating remain. The dataset, benchmark website, and codebase are publicly available.
nodes.subject: Computation and Language

nodes.title: MIC-BEV: Multi-Infrastructure Camera Bird's-Eye-View Transformer with Relation-Aware Fusion for 3D Object Detection
nodes.authors: Yun Zhang, Zhaoliang Zheng, Johnson Liu, Zhiyu Huang, Zewei Zhou, Zonglin Meng, Tianhui Cai, Jiaqi Ma
nodes.summary: Infrastructure-based perception plays a crucial role in intelligent transportation systems by providing global situational awareness and enabling cooperative autonomy. However, camera-based 3D object detection remains challenging under multi-view infrastructure setups, heterogeneous camera configurations, degraded sensing conditions, diverse road layouts, and adverse environmental conditions. We introduce MIC-BEV, a Transformer-based bird's-eye-view (BEV) perception framework for infrastructure-based multi-camera 3D object detection. MIC-BEV supports a variable number of cameras with heterogeneous intrinsic and extrinsic parameters and uses a graph-enhanced fusion module to adaptively integrate multi-view image features by modeling geometric relationships between cameras and the BEV grid. To support training and evaluation, we introduce M2I, a synthetic dataset featuring diverse camera layouts, road geometries, environmental conditions, and sensor-degradation cases. Experiments on the simulated M2I dataset and the real-world RoScenes dataset show that MIC-BEV achieves strong 3D detection performance and improved robustness under challenging conditions. Ablation studies validate the effectiveness of its key design choices, while weight analyses show that the learned fusion weights are associated with view-reliability factors and adapt to degraded camera inputs. We further report computational cost and deployment-related factors, providing additional evidence of practical feasibility and real-world deployment potential. These results indicate that MIC-BEV is a promising framework for infrastructure-based perception. The dataset and source code are available at: https://github.com/HandsomeYun/MIC-BEV.
nodes.subject: 3D Vision

nodes.title: Kineo: Calibration-Free Metric Motion Capture From Sparse RGB Cameras
nodes.authors: Charles Javerliat, Pierre Raimbaud, Guillaume Lavoué
nodes.summary: Markerless multi-view motion capture is often constrained by the need for precise camera calibration, limiting accessibility for non-experts and in-the-wild captures. Existing calibration-free approaches mitigate this requirement but suffer from high computational cost and reduced reconstruction accuracy. We present Kineo, a fully automatic, calibration-free pipeline for markerless motion capture from videos captured by unsynchronized, uncalibrated, consumer-grade RGB cameras. Kineo leverages 2D keypoints from off-the-shelf detectors to simultaneously calibrate cameras, including Brown-Conrady distortion coefficients, and reconstruct 3D keypoints and dense scene pointmaps at metric scale. A confidence-aware spatio-temporal keypoint subsampling strategy, combined with graph-based global optimization, enables robust calibration at a fixed computational cost independent of sequence length. We further introduce a pairwise reprojection consistency score, a heuristic measure of the agreement between views, which we use to weight bone lengths in metric scale recovery. Evaluations on EgoHumans and Human3.6M demonstrate substantial improvements over prior calibration-free methods. Compared to previous state-of-the-art approaches, Kineo reduces camera translation error by approximately 83-85%, camera angular error by 86-92%, and world mean-per-joint position error (W-MPJPE) by 83-91%. Kineo is also efficient in real-world scenarios, processing multi-view sequences faster than their duration in a specific configuration (e.g., 36 min to process 1 h 23 min of footage). The full pipeline and evaluation code are openly released to promote reproducibility and practical adoption at: https://liris-xr.github.io/kineo/
nodes.subject: 3D Vision

nodes.title: InFeR: Informed Failure Resilience in Learned Visual Navigation Control
nodes.authors: Zishuo Wang, Joel Loo, David Hsu
nodes.summary: While imitation learning (IL) has enabled successful visual navigation in many common environments, IL policies are prone to unpredictable failures under out-of-distribution (OOD) scenarios. This necessitates failure-resilient policies, which not only detect failures, but also recognise their sources and recover from them autonomously. We propose InFeR, a general framework for building IL policies with informed failure resilience without failure or recovery demonstrations. Given an IL policy's architecture and training dataset, InFeR retrains a new OOD-aware policy with a latent space structured for OOD failure detection, with a modified objective based on the Variational Information Bottleneck. It applies a visual explainability technique, Grad-CAM, to attribute failures to specific image regions and inform a heuristic policy for recovery. All these are achieved without requiring additional training data. Real-world experiments show that InFeR enables informed failure recovery across two different policy architectures, supporting long-range navigation in complex environments.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: Manifold Approximation leads to Robust Kernel Alignment
nodes.authors: Mohammad Tariqul Islam, Du Liu, Deblina Sarkar
nodes.summary: Centered kernel alignment (CKA) is a popular metric for comparing representations, determining equivalence of networks, and conducting neuroscience research. However, CKA does not account for the underlying manifold and relies on numerous heuristics that cause it to behave differently at different scales of data. In this work, we propose Manifold-approximated Kernel Alignment (MKA), which incorporates manifold geometry (i.e., local neighborhood) into the alignment task. We derive a theoretical framework for MKA. Our construction removes representation-dependent degree weighting, yields a closed-form alignment score, and gives each row a probabilistic interpretation as a local Markov transition distribution. We further establish kernel- and score-level stability with respect to the neighborhood size. We perform empirical evaluations on synthetic datasets and real-world examples to characterize and compare MKA to its contemporaries. In controlled synthetic experiments, MKA is consistently less sensitive to hyperparameters and captures the selected topology-preserving relationships. On the large-scale benchmark, MKA achieves its strongest aggregate performance in vision, is competitive on graphs, and is weaker than CKA in several NLP evaluations. Our findings suggest that manifold-aware kernel alignment provides a robust foundation for measuring representations and is potentially useful when local neighborhood geometry is important, with possible applications in representation learning.
nodes.subject: LLM Agents with Reinforcement Learning

nodes.title: Revisiting Value Iteration: Unified Analysis of Discounted and Average-Reward Cases
nodes.authors: Arsenii Mustafin, Xinyi Sheng, Dominik Baumann
nodes.summary: While Value Iteration (VI) is one of the most fundamental algorithms in Reinforcement Learning, its theoretical convergence guarantees still exhibit a persistent mismatch with empirical behavior. In the discounted-reward case, classical theory guarantees geometric convergence with rate $γ$, while in the average-reward case recent work suggests that only sublinear convergence can be expected. In practice, however, VI is often observed to converge significantly faster. In this work, we show through a unified geometry-based analysis that, under an assumption of a unique and unichain optimal policy, (i) convergence is geometric in both the discounted- and average-reward settings and (ii) the convergence rate is faster than previous analyses suggest.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: DeepfakeBench-MM: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Multimodal Deepfake Detection
nodes.authors: Kangran Zhao, Xiaoyu Zhang, Yupeng Chen, Yize Chen, Weinan Guan, Bo Zheng, Yufan Liao, Chengzhe Sun, Soumyya Kanti Datta, Qingshan Liu, Siwei Lyu, Baoyuan Wu
nodes.summary: Audio-visual deepfakes can spread misinformation and enable impersonation, undermining trust in digital media. However, existing datasets provide limited coverage of forgery operations and their combinations, constraining detector development and systematic evaluation. We introduce Mega-MMDF, containing 100,000 real and 1.2 million forged clips across 22 pipelines spanning modality-specific manipulations, stacked forgeries, and joint audio-video generation. To assess its training value and enable fair comparisons, we develop DeepfakeBench-MM, which standardizes training and evaluation across 8 datasets and 10 detectors. Training-based detectors achieve their highest mean AUC when trained on Mega-MMDF, with gains of up to 0.0784 over the best alternative training dataset for each detector. Experiments on data scale and pipeline coverage further support the value of large, diverse training data. Cross-pipeline evaluations reveal bidirectional and asymmetric generalization. Training on composite forgeries does not necessarily enable detection of their constituent operations in isolation. Our analysis of altered inputs shows that modality masking can increase false alarms and missed detections, and temporal misalignment can raise mean predicted forgery probabilities. Together, these resources provide a foundation for understanding and improving multimodal deepfake detection, with publicly available code and dataset access subject to application and usage terms.
nodes.subject: Multimedia

nodes.title: Mega-MMDF and DeepfakeBench-MM: Benchmarking Multimodal Deepfake Detection Across Diverse Forgery Pipelines
nodes.authors: Kangran Zhao, Xiaoyu Zhang, Yupeng Chen, Yize Chen, Weinan Guan, Bo Zheng, Yufan Liao, Chengzhe Sun, Soumyya Kanti Datta, Qingshan Liu, Siwei Lyu, Baoyuan Wu

nodes.subject: Digital Human

nodes.title: AI-Mediated Communication Can Reduce Opinion-Based Network Segregation
nodes.authors: Faria Huq, Elijah L. Claggett, Hirokazu Shirado
nodes.summary: Everyday communication is increasingly AI-mediated, with large language models (LLMs) suggesting wording, tone, and framing while humans decide whether to adopt them. Because communication can shape who people choose to interact with, the effects of AI mediation may extend beyond individual attitudes and perceptions to broader patterns of network segregation across opinion differences. Here, we examine this possibility through a preregistered online experiment (N=711 across 80 sessions) in which participants discussed controversial political topics over multiple rounds and could freely reorganize into groups. During the discussions, participants received LLM-generated message suggestions under either individual AI assistance centered on participants' own stances or relational AI assistance incorporating group members' perspectives. We find that individual and relational AI assistance produced distinct trajectories of opinion-based network segregation. Segregation remained largely unchanged under individual AI assistance but decreased significantly under relational AI assistance. Even though many participants adopted few or no AI-generated suggestions, relational AI assistance significantly increased positive sentiment in group discussions. More positive conversations then helped sustain more opinion-diverse groups. The relational communication strategy had no detectable network-level effect when presented as direct instruction to participants, suggesting that AI scaffolding contributed to the observed reduction in segregation. Incorporating the perspectives of social partners into AI-mediated communication can reduce opinion-based network segregation.
nodes.subject: Generative Search Engines

nodes.title: AuthRank: Scoring Source Credibility to Counter Poisoning in CTI LLM Pipelines
nodes.authors: Austin Jia, Avaneesh Ramesh, Zain Shamsi, Daniel Zhang, Alex Liu
nodes.summary: Large Language Model (LLM) pipelines have become essential for processing Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) to quickly extract updated threat information from open source feeds and reports for real time processing. However, these pipelines are susceptible to poisoning attacks, and previously proposed defenses can fail for CTI contexts as cyber threat information is often completely novel, and attackers can easily mimic the stylistic conventions. We propose that the robustness of LLM pipelines can be improved by applying source credibility algorithms on document corpora, using PageRank as an example. We introduce AuthRank, a credibility score computed from citation networks built using explicit citations, LLM-inferred citations, and claim-level entailment, enhanced with time decay and author credibility. Our experiments on the standardized MS MARCO dataset demonstrate improved accuracy under poisoning, and we show proof-of-concept performance on CTI documents and feeds.
nodes.subject: Information Retrieval

nodes.title: On the Structure of Stationary Solutions to McKean-Vlasov Equations with Applications to Noisy Transformers
nodes.authors: Krishnakumar Balasubramanian, Sayan Banerjee, Philippe Rigollet
nodes.summary: We study stationary solutions of McKean-Vlasov equations on the circle. We establish an exact equivalence between solutions of the stationary McKean-Vlasov equation and an infinite-dimensional quadratic system of equations over Fourier coefficients, allowing explicit characterization of stationary states in a sequence space rather than a function space. This framework provides a transparent description of local bifurcations, their periodicity and resonance structures, while accommodating singular potentials. We derive analytic expressions for the emergence, form and shape (supercritical, critical, subcritical or transcritical) of bifurcations involving possibly multiple Fourier modes and connect them with discontinuous phase transitions. We also characterize, under suitable assumptions, the detailed structure of the stationary bifurcating solutions through leading small-amplitude coefficients for arbitrarily many fixed Fourier modes. At the global level, we establish regularity and concavity properties of the free energy landscape, proving existence, compactness, and coexistence of globally minimizing stationary measures, and identifying discontinuous phase transitions with points of non-differentiability of the minimum free energy map. We apply the theory to the Noisy Mean-Field Transformer model, where we show how changing the inverse temperature $β$ affects the geometry of the infinitely many bifurcations from the uniform measure. We also discuss how increasing $β$ motivates the study of approximate multi-mode stationary profiles as candidates for a separate metastability analysis; persistence times require additional dynamical estimates. Moreover, we determine the exact threshold $β_0\simeq2.447$ separating continuous and discontinuous phase transitions in this model. The same threshold marks the change of the first bifurcation from supercritical to subcritical.
nodes.subject: LLM Agents with Reinforcement Learning

nodes.title: ALICE-LRI: A General Method for Lossless Range Image Generation for Spinning LiDAR Sensors without Calibration Metadata
nodes.authors: Samuel Soutullo, Miguel Yermo, David L. Vilariño, Óscar G. Lorenzo, José C. Cabaleiro, Francisco F. Rivera
nodes.summary: 3D LiDAR sensors are widely used in autonomous navigation, environmental monitoring, and precision mapping. Their point clouds are often projected into 2D range images for efficient processing, but conventional projection methods can lose points because of geometric inconsistencies. We present ALICE-LRI (Automatic LiDAR Intrinsic Calibration Estimation for Lossless Range Images), a metadata-free method for lossless range-image generation from calibrated spinning multi-beam LiDAR point clouds. It requires neither factory calibration files, packet-level data, nor beam identifiers, and targets operating regimes where scanlines contain enough returns for reliable parameter estimation. The method estimates the intrinsic calibration parameters relevant to projection, including beam configuration, angular distributions, and per-beam geometric corrections. Evaluation on the complete KITTI and DurLAR datasets yielded zero lost points across all point clouds. Reconstruction deviations remain below manufacturer-reported range-performance specifications, while the method runs in real time. A compression case study also shows improved reconstruction quality and a better quality-compression trade-off for a downstream application. These results enable range-image-based LiDAR processing in applications that require high measurement fidelity and preservation of acquired geometric information.
nodes.subject: Robotics

nodes.title: CS-54k: A Paper-Grounded Corpus and Benchmark for AI Research QA
nodes.authors: Penghao Wang, Yuhao Zhou, Mengxuan Wu, Ziheng Qin, Bangyuan Zhu, Shengbin Huang, Xuanlei Zhao, Panpan Zhang, Xiaojiang Peng, Yuzhang Shang, Jianfei Yang, Zheng Zhu, Tianlong Chen, Zhangyang Wang, Kai Wang
nodes.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being used to support computer science research. To contribute reliably, these systems must be able to work with information distributed across research papers and across different aspects of the research process. However, large-scale resources that systematically organize such information into structured supervision for both model evaluation and post-training remain limited. To address this gap, we propose a systematic paper-to-QA construction pipeline that organizes information from AI research papers into structured QA pairs supported by source evidence. Using this pipeline, we construct CS-54k, a 54k-pair corpus derived from 14,474 openly licensed AI research papers. The corpus covers eight recurring paper components, including research domain, prior work, existing challenges, motivation, findings and assumptions, methods, experimental settings, and experimental results. We further derive two complementary subsets: CS-4k, a benchmark for evaluating LLMs on paper-derived research QA, and CS-50k, a companion corpus for post-training. Extensive evaluations on CS-4k reveal substantial performance differences across existing LLMs and paper components, with experimental settings and results remaining particularly challenging. Moreover, post-training on CS-50k substantially improves Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct on CS-4k, demonstrating the practical utility of structured, paper-derived supervision. Together, CS-4k and CS-50k provide a unified and scalable resource for benchmarking and improving LLMs on research paper question answering.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: Interpret Policies in Deep Reinforcement Learning using SILVER with RL-Guided Labeling: A Model-level Approach to High-dimensional and Multi-action Environments
nodes.authors: Yiyu Qian, Liyuan Zhao
nodes.summary: Deep reinforcement learning (RL) achieves remarkable performance but lacks interpretability, limiting trust in policy behavior. The existing SILVER framework (Li, Siddique, and Cao 2025) explains RL policy via Shapley-based regression but remains restricted to low-dimensional, binary-action domains. We propose SILVER with RL-guided labeling, an enhanced variant that extends SILVER to multi-action and high-dimensional environments by incorporating the RL policy's own action outputs into the boundary points identification. Our method first extracts compact feature representations from image observations, performs SHAP-based feature attribution, and then employs RL-guided labeling to generate behaviorally consistent boundary datasets. Surrogate models, such as decision trees and regression-based functions, are subsequently trained to interpret RL policy's decision structure. We evaluate the proposed framework on two Atari environments using three deep RL algorithms and conduct human-subject study to assess the clarity and trustworthiness of the derived interpretable policy. Results show that our approach maintains competitive task performance while substantially improving transparency and human understanding of agent behavior. This work advances explainable RL by transforming SILVER into a scalable and behavior-aware framework for interpreting deep RL agents in high-dimensional, multi-action settings.
nodes.subject: Generative POI Search and Recommendation

nodes.title: Survival of the fittest Cox model: Pivotal variable selection for time-to-event data
nodes.authors: Maxime van Cutsem, Sylvain Sardy
nodes.summary: We revisit Cox's proportional hazards model to improve variable selection in survival analysis. A square-root transformation of the partial likelihood renders the selection of the regularization parameter asymptotically pivotal: the baseline hazard and the censoring rate cancel exactly, and the way censoring is spread over time only enters through a bounded correction of order $1/\log n$. Using martingale residuals, we compute this penalty level by Monte Carlo without reordering the design matrix. The resulting criterion borrows from information criteria such as BIC and from penalized regression methods such as the lasso, taking the best of both. On simulated and real data, our method substantially improves upon state-of-the-art approaches used daily.
nodes.subject: Machine Learning

nodes.title: DualHash: Stochastic Primal-Dual Algorithms for W-Type Regularized Deep Hashing
nodes.authors: Luxuan Li, Xiao Wang, Chunfeng Cui
nodes.summary: Deep hashing encodes high-dimensional image features into compact binary codes, enabling efficient similarity search in large-scale content-based image retrieval, a problem akin to semantic-preserving lossy compression under extreme bit-rate constraints. A fundamental challenge in deep hashing stems from the discrete nature of quantization in generating the codes. W-type regularizations, such as $z\mapsto\||z|-1\|_1$, are widely adopted and empirically effective at pushing network outputs toward binary values. However, existing methods often directly optimize these regularizations without convergence guarantees. While proximal gradient methods offer a promising solution, the coupling between W-type regularizers and neural network outputs results in composite forms that generally lack closed-form proximal solutions. In this paper, using Fenchel duality, we reformulate the nonconvex W-type regularization term through its convex conjugate, yielding a min-max problem with tractable proximal updates. We show that this min-max problem captures the stationarity of the original deep hashing objective up to the quantization error. Building on this problem, we present a stochastic primal-dual hashing algorithm, referred to as DualHash, with oracle complexity guarantees. We derive two algorithm instances: a momentum-based version with $O(\varepsilon^{-4})$ oracle complexity and an improved $O(\varepsilon^{-3})$ version using variance reduction, both for $\varepsilon$-KKT points of the min-max problem, which yield near-stationarity guarantees for the original objective. Experiments on three standard datasets demonstrate competitive retrieval accuracy and reduced quantization error, validating the practical value of DualHash for image retrieval problems. Our implementation of DualHash is available at https://github.com/RailLee/DualHash.
nodes.subject: NeRF

nodes.title: Investigating LLM Capabilities on Long Context Comprehension for Clinical Question Answering
nodes.authors: Feras AlMannaa, Talia Tseriotou, Jenny Chim, Maria Liakata
nodes.summary: Despite the impressive reported performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) on medical Question-Answering (QA), evaluation still overrelies on multiple-choice and extractive settings primarily assessing textbook knowledge, with limited work on open-ended QA over patient records. We present a comprehensive study investigating LLM long-context (LC) comprehension on longitudinal, patient-centric Electronic Health Records (EHRs) across multiple datasets, models and metrics, covering extractive, multiple-choice, and open-ended generative QA under different context formulation and Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) settings. We show that medically fine-tuned models offer no measurable benefit over base counterparts, smaller models exhibit stronger memorization, and longitudinal supplementary notes aid generative QA. Reasoning models gain on complex multi-note QA under LLM Correctness but not stricter reference-aligned metrics, while hybrid RAG with reranking outperforms Full-Context (FC) prompting. A question-category analysis and multi-faceted metric evaluation further reveal where RAG and FC excel and struggle, with RAG falling behind in longitudinal reasoning, thus uncovering systematic failures pointing to the need for reasoning-appropriate metrics.
nodes.subject: Computation and Language

nodes.title: DualHash: Stochastic Primal-Dual Algorithms for W-Type Regularized Deep Hashing
nodes.authors: Luxuan Li, Xiao Wang, Chunfeng Cui
nodes.summary: Deep hashing encodes high-dimensional image features into compact binary codes, enabling efficient similarity search in large-scale content-based image retrieval, a problem akin to semantic-preserving lossy compression under extreme bit-rate constraints.
